articles.title: Police ramp up road-safety ops with drone crackdown
articles.excerpt: Police say drones recorded 42 instances of drivers crossing double white lines on two winding roads in Southern District on…
articles.fullText:
Police say drones recorded 42 instances of drivers crossing double white lines on two winding roads in Southern District on Saturday.

The footage was captured on Stanley Gap Road and Victoria Road as part of the law enforcement's day-long operation, code-named "Torch", targeting illegal racing and dangerous driving.

Acting Chief Inspector Wong Ka-wing said police would keep up the pressure on reckless drivers.

"In this operation, we deployed drones to make recordings, allowing us to gather evidence effectively while reducing the impact on other road users," Wong said.

"Police will continue to carry out intelligence-led operations at unannounced times, using drones and other technology, to crack down hard on driving that endangers road safety."

Wong warned offenders could face more than just a ticket.

Under the Road Traffic Ordinance, those convicted of dangerous driving face a fine of up to HK$25,000 and three years' imprisonment.

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Asian infrastructure bank to set up office in HK
articles.excerpt: The world’s second-largest multilateral development bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, will set up an office in Hong Kong, the…
articles.fullText:
The world’s second-largest multilateral development bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, will set up an office in Hong Kong, the government announced on Saturday.

This follows the signing of two agreements between the bank and the central and Hong Kong governments on Saturday, with the first paving the way for the bank to establish its presence in the SAR.

Hong Kong has been a member of the 111-member bank since 2017.

Speaking at the signing ceremony, Financial Secretary Paul Chan thanked the bank for placing its trust in Hong Kong.

“The bank's decision is a resounding vote of confidence in our city as an international financial centre," he said.

"A presence here will also allow Hong Kong to contribute more directly, on multiple fronts, to the bank's work.

“The new office will give Hong Kong's financial community more direct access to the bank and its specialists.

"This will make it easier for both sides to discuss project proposals, identify opportunities to work together and draw on local professional expertise as projects move from planning to implementation.”

The SAR is also committed to working more closely with the bank on talent development, capacity building and capital market access, Chan added.

Under the second agreement, Hong Kong will contribute a further US$20 million to the bank's project preparation special fund, double its initial contribution of US$10 million in 2018.

The fund provides grants for early-stage work on infrastructure projects. By September, it had approved US$110 million in grants for 45 projects across 13 member economies.

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Court backs Bayer's US$7.25b Roundup cancer payout
articles.excerpt: A US judge has approved Bayer's US$7.25 billion settlement of lawsuits over claims its Roundup weedkiller caused blood cancer, in…
articles.fullText:
A US judge has approved Bayer's US$7.25 billion settlement of lawsuits over claims its Roundup weedkiller caused blood cancer, in one of the largest class-action payouts in US history.

Friday's decision paves the way for compensation to tens of thousands of people who were exposed to the glyphosate-based herbicide and have been diagnosed with Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL).

It also covers people who were exposed to Roundup and go on to develop the illness in the future.

The Missouri state court "fully and finally approves the settlement agreement in its entirety," judge Timothy Boyer said in his ruling.

"Today is a real good day," Christopher Seeger, a court-appointed lead attorney for plaintiffs already diagnosed with NHL, said.

People with diagnosed NHL will receive payments of between US$10,000 and US$165,000, depending on a range of factors including whether they were residential or occupational users of Roundup, such as landscapers.

Approval of the settlement was "really the only path that most victims of Roundup will have to compensation," Seeger said, because in June, the US Supreme Court sided with Bayer in a case and ruled it would no longer allow "failure-to-warn" claims in US states.

The top court concluded that the US Environmental Protection Agency's determination that Roundup is not a carcinogen pre-empts claims in state courts tying the product to a cancer diagnosis.

Seeger explained that those claims had been the most viable path for most plaintiffs. This settlement was reached before the Supreme Court ruling, but both sides had agreed to honour it whatever the outcome.

People who never filed a case but were exposed to Roundup can still apply for compensation if they develop NHL in the coming years and if they meet certain conditions.

Bayer has spent billions of dollars settling thousands of cases linked to Roundup since it acquired the weedkiller's producer, the US agrichemical group Monsanto, in 2018. In a statement, the company said it hoped the settlement, together with the Supreme Court decision, would help draw a line under litigation.

"The court's final approval is a decisive milestone in the company's strategy to mitigate the risks of both pending and future Roundup litigation," said CEO Bill Anderson. (AFP)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Trump credits Xi for 'immaculate' Shenzhen development
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump praised Shenzhen as "immaculate" while contrasting the metropolis to the conditions of American cities during a…
articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump praised Shenzhen as "immaculate" while contrasting the metropolis to the conditions of American cities during a White House news conference.

Speaking shortly after returning to Washington, DC, from the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit, he noted the city's growth from a fishing village not long ago, crediting President Xi Jinping for the development.

"What a job President Xi has done, it's clean it's immaculate, it's been built in a short period of time," said Trump.

"And when I look at our cities, they're dirty, I must say, mostly blue [Democrat-controlled] ...and they have potholes all over the place. Railings are falling down, and everything is rusty and disgusting and the crime is through the roof."

The US leader also highlighted the energy of Shenzhen residents, which he said he had noticed after touring around the city.

Reflecting on the trilateral summit with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin, Trump said the meetings had "great electricity" and that they discussed cooperation to limit the spread of nuclear weapons. (With contributions from AFP)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Rosanna Law confident of beating 53.8m visitors target
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism Rosanna Law said she is confident Hong Kong will exceed its target of 53.8…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism Rosanna Law said she is confident Hong Kong will exceed its target of 53.8 million visitor arrivals this year.

Speaking on a Commercial Radio programme on Saturday, she said the recent Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings in Shenzhen had brought more visitors, including officials and business leaders, to the city,

Some hotels in Tsim Sha Tsui had, she added, reported occupancy rates of almost 92 percent.

The city recorded 45.8 million visitor arrivals in the first 10 months of the year, up 12 percent year on year.

"With two months left, I'm quite confident growth won't be lower than eight percent," Law said, with the government having forecast growth of about eight percent this year.

"If so, we'll end the year above our original forecast."

Law added that she is fairly confident arrivals could reach 55 million by end of the year as November and December are typically peak months.

She also said the "ticket stub economy" is gradually spreading to other districts.

Businesses around the Mong Kok Flower Market are, for example, offering special deals during the Hong Kong Premier League football season.

Under the scheme, which ends on December 19, event tickets also work as discount vouchers at partner restaurants, malls and bars. The idea is to spread visitor spending beyond sporting venues such as Mong Kok Stadium.

Law said the scheme might take time to catch on across districts, as it did at Kai Tak, but called it a "good start".

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Whiz 'used Claude to prove Millennium math hypothesis'
articles.excerpt: A researcher at AI company Anthropic says he has used the firm's Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a…
articles.fullText:
A researcher at AI company Anthropic says he has used the firm's Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.

First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics.

"I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis," Levent Alpoge wrote in a four-page note released on Friday.

The claim has not been independently verified, and the proof has not yet been reviewed by outside experts.

"It's a monumental moment in human history. It's really the biggest thing I think that's ever happened in mathematics," said Brian Conrey, a leading specialist on the Riemann Hypothesis.

"I really did not see this coming at all," he said, adding that he had not yet seen a manuscript, only the remarks Alpoge posted on his website, and had asked for a copy.

"It looks like it's seriously complicated. I don't think any human was about to find this," Conrey said, adding that he believed "there will be simpler ways to do it."

Hours after Alpoge's announcement, Stanford University mathematics professor Ravi Vakil said a postdoctoral researcher in the same department had independently submitted a proof of the hypothesis.

The Riemann Hypothesis is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000, which offers US$1 million for a solution to each.

Under the institute's rules, a solution must be published in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand two years of scrutiny.

Alpoge said the method also resolves a broader version of the problem known as the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis.

He said he with help of Claude had produced a version of the proof in Lean, a programming language that allows mathematical arguments to be checked by computer, and that he was releasing only that version for now.

A full written argument would be extremely long, he said, adding that he had not yet mastered all of the mathematics involved and planned to write it up properly.

Alpoge said he had consulted Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei before announcing the result, and acknowledged that its timing could be viewed cynically, without elaborating. The announcement came the day after Anthropic's record stock market debut.

In August, Anthropic said an unreleased version of Claude had improved a long-standing result related to the Riemann Hypothesis, while stressing that it had not proved it.

The claim comes two months after rival OpenAI said an AI model had solved another Millennium Prize Problem, on the equations that govern how fluids move. Mathematicians say that proof appears correct but has yet to be fully vetted. (AFP)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Ex-Uber driver convicted of starting LA Palisades fire
articles.excerpt: A US jury has convicted a man of setting a New Year's Eve fire that grew into one of several…
articles.fullText:
A US jury has convicted a man of setting a New Year's Eve fire that grew into one of several deadly 2025 blazes in Los Angeles, killing 12 people in the Pacific Palisades.

It was the second federal trial of Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, after the initial prosecution attempt left the jury deadlocked and ended in a mistrial.

The former Uber driver is scheduled for sentencing on March 17. He faces up to 40 years in prison.

Earlier this year, a separate jury leaned 10-2 towards acquitting Rinderknecht, but verdicts must be reached unanimously.

Jurors in the second trial were ordered not to take the previous proceedings or any mention of them into account in reaching their decision.

Friday's verdict was on two charges: destruction of property by means of fire and arson affecting property used in interstate commerce.

But after approximately two days of deliberations, jurors found he used a lighter to ignite a brush fire in the vicinity of the wealthy, Malibu-adjacent Pacific Palisades neighbourhood.

Firefighters had thought they extinguished the blaze, but later found that smouldering embers underground were carried by strong winds and erupted, tearing through the affluent area and ravaging thousands of homes.

It proved to be among the most destructive wildfires in California history.

Rinderknecht's defence attorney, Steven Haney, had argued there was no direct evidence that his client started the fire, and suggested errant New Year's Eve fireworks could be to blame.

He said phone record evidence that Rinderknecht called 911 were efforts that he was trying to help alleviate the situation.

But the prosecution said evidence including cell phone data put him at the scene of the crime.

They also pointed to a combination of video surveillance footage and analysis of fire spread dynamics to insist on his guilt.

The prosecution also said that Rinderknecht asked ChatGPT whether someone could be held liable for starting a fire with cigarettes.

One of the jurors, who identified himself as Cameron, said outside the courthouse that while he had originally leaned not guilty, Rinderknecht's interview with federal investigators was incriminating.

"It was a clear, calm night. You know, no one else was on that hill that day, or that day or night," the juror said, but the defendant "happened to be smoking, and because he happened to be smoking, he had a lighter."

"Everything kind of started to point towards one conclusion."

Bill Essayli, who leads the US Attorney's Office for the Central District of California, lauded the verdict as "a measure of justice for the families who lost loved ones and the thousands whose lives were upended."

Fierce winds fuelled the 2025 Los Angeles fires that resulted in a total of 31 deaths. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Father arrested over son's alleged fake-label goods op
articles.excerpt: Customs officers have arrested an online shop worker and seized about HK$500,000 worth of suspected counterfeit perfumes and toys. The…
articles.fullText:
Customs officers have arrested an online shop worker and seized about HK$500,000 worth of suspected counterfeit perfumes and toys.

The arrest follows a raid on an industrial building unit in Kwun Tong last week as part of an operation against counterfeit goods.

Officers suspect a 30-year-old man, who is not in Hong Kong, has been running two online shops selling the alleged counterfeit products since 2023. The arrested worker is his father.

Officers allege the 61-year-old assisted with daily operations and handled HK$6 million in profits from the sale of the suspected fake goods.

"Preliminary investigations show that the suspect is responsible for the daily storage and delivery of a distribution centre," said Liu Man-chun, an inspector in the intellectual property technology crime investigation unit, adding that he is currently out on bail.

"Subsequent investigations also revealed that the person in charge of the online store in the case is a 30-year-old local man, the son of the arrested man.

"The case is still under investigation. We won't rule out the possibility of further arrests."

Liu alleged that the counterfeiters copied the designs and registered trademarks of genuine brand products, making it difficult for customers to discern whether they were fake.

He said consumers could tell the difference because the lettering on a genuine perfume bottle was clear and sharp, while fake ones appeared blurry.

Liu said government laboratories would test the confiscated perfume to ensure it posed no health risks.

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: 'China, Russia, US consensus positive for HK economy'
articles.excerpt: Commerce Secretary Algernon Yau said on Saturday that the joint declaration of peace issued by President Xi Jinping and his…
articles.fullText:
Commerce Secretary Algernon Yau said on Saturday that the joint declaration of peace issued by President Xi Jinping and his Russian and US counterparts, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump, is positive for the world economy and Hong Kong.

The three leaders released the declaration following trilateral talks on the sidelines of the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen.

Speaking on RTHK, Yau said the consensus reached by the major powers would support global stability and trade.

"In the meeting between the leaders of China, Russia and the United States, they all hoped to reach a consensus on building a peaceful world, resolving conflicts in the world and creating a prosperous global economy through cooperation," he said.

"The consensus reached by the three major countries will have an impact on the future global economy, including Hong Kong's economy."

During his keynote speech at the Apec CEO Summit, Xi said China supports establishing a world association for bay area economic cooperation to deepen exchanges between such areas and strengthen Asia-Pacific economic ties.

Yau said that as a key city in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, Hong Kong plays a vital role in helping the region connect with other bay areas worldwide, such as those in Japan and the United States.

The SAR can contribute, he said, by leveraging its advantages as an international centre for trade, shipping and finance.

"I think the opportunities are enormous," Yau said.

"If these bay areas can connect and boost trade, it will greatly expand import-export activity, personnel exchanges and talent complementarity."

During the Apec summit, Chief Executive John Lee also held bilateral talks with leaders from seven economies: Malaysia, Vietnam, Brunei, Thailand, Chile, Peru and Singapore.

Yau said the discussions focused on cooperation in areas such as education and trade, while also touching on tariffs and the avoidance of double taxation.

He said the chief executive also briefed the leaders about opportunities in the Northern Metropolis.

In meetings with leaders from Asean members, Lee also discussed Hong Kong's bid to join the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, Yau added.

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto rakes in almost US$3.8bn on first day
articles.excerpt: "Grand Theft Auto VI" brought in US$3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, publisher Rockstar Games said on…
articles.fullText:
"Grand Theft Auto VI" brought in US$3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, publisher Rockstar Games said on Friday, calling it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history.

The figure, based on company estimates of worldwide sales through the end of Thursday, is nearly five times the roughly US$800 million that predecessor "Grand Theft Auto V" took in during its first 24 hours in 2013.

Rockstar, a label of New York-based Take-Two Interactive, said the game had sold 32.5 million units before release, a record across all platforms.

"We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world," said Sam Houser, the studio's founder and president.

The game came out on Thursday on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. It launched first at midnight in New Zealand and then rolled out to each market as the clock reached midnight there.

The release generated more social media posts than this year's World Cup, according to monitoring platform Visibrain.

Critics praised the game, which has a score of 99 on review aggregator Metacritic. Rockstar said that made it the highest-rated game ever.

In a review for The Verge, Andrew Webster wrote that "the game is so good that the outsize hype is the least interesting thing about it."

This week the game received eight nominations for the Game Awards, which will be held December 10.

Rockstar spent more than eight years developing the title. It delayed the launch twice, first from autumn 2025 and then from May 2026.

The studio was also hit by a 2022 hack in which stolen gameplay footage was posted online.

The series has long been accused of glorifying violence and crime. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Harry Kane out 'for months' with ankle injury
articles.excerpt: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is set to be out for "months" with an ankle injury, Bayern Munich coach Vincent…
articles.fullText:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is set to be out for "months" with an ankle injury, Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany said on Friday.

England captain Kane was subbed out early in the Bayern's 1-1 Bundesliga home draw against Cologne after a tackle with Kompany telling Sky Germany the forward would to be out for "months" rather than "weeks". (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Tech stocks slump, leaving Nasdaq in red for the year
articles.excerpt: A bruising sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks on Friday pulled the S&P 500 down 3.7 percent, dragging the index to…
articles.fullText:
A bruising sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks on Friday pulled the S&P 500 down 3.7 percent, dragging the index to its worst weekly loss in more than 18 months, and knocking the Nasdaq composite into the red for the year.

The S&P 500 fell 265.44 points to 6,910.39. The Dow dropped 949.73 points to 48,147.33, and the Nasdaq lost 1,261.47 points to close at 22,617.73.

The benchmark index is now in what professional investors call a “correction,” having fallen more than 10 percent from its October 6 all-time high.

The last time the S&P 500 had a correction was March 2025, as the Trump administration’s trade war rattled the market. Its weekly loss, marking its worst such decline since April 2025, as the trade war escalated, capped a seven-day losing streak, the longest such string of losses since the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020.

The Nasdaq composite slumped 5.3 percent, pulling it into negative territory for the year. Its weekly loss was also just shy of its worst week since March 2020.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average, with less exposure to technology stocks, fell 1.9 percent.

Chip stocks like Nvidia, Micron Technology, Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices bore the brunt of the selling, but other companies connected to the AI buildout tanked as well, including the optical products company Corning and the energy provider Bloom Energy. The AI lab Anthropic, coming off a successful IPO Thursday, tumbled 9.1 percent.

The AI trade has been losing steam partly over worries that AI stocks’ big market values and heavy spending are unjustified. Fears of a bubble within the sector have also been exacerbated by the results of the recent midterm elections, with candidates advocating for a slowdown in data centre construction winning at both the federal and state level.

“The whole notion that AI can continue to spend unlimited amounts of money and support the stock market, I think the notion of that is ending as we speak, that’s what’s being priced right now,” said Michael Antonelli, market strategist at Baird. “But I don’t think that means that the overall bull market that started in October 2022 is over.”

Much of the AI rout was centred among chip stocks, which have been big beneficiaries of the build out of AI data centres. Advanced Micro Devices sank 13.3 percent, Micron Technology slid 13.9 percent and Broadcom fell 12.1 percent.

Nvidia, considered by many to be the poster child for the AI boom, fell for the ninth day in the last 10, closing 13.8 percent lower. The chip company’s stock was caught up in the market’s anxiety about the strength of the AI build out, and more recently has been pressured by worries about its future following the sudden downfall of Jensen Huang, its former CEO and co-founder. Since the Huang scandal erupted earlier this month, the stock has dropped more than 25 percent.

The big market debut for Anthropic, maker of the Claude AI tool, fizzled on Friday with the rest of the tech sector. The stock fell 9.1 percent to US$88.30, but remains above its IPO price of US$83 per share. It was the biggest public stock offering ever, at one point surpassing US$2 trillion in value. (AP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: UK, EU hail new deals 10 years after Brexit
articles.excerpt: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU's top officials on Friday sealed deals at a Brussels summit to ease…
articles.fullText:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU's top officials on Friday sealed deals at a Brussels summit to ease trade and youth mobility after Brexit, but kicked down the road the question of where ties go next.

Burnham has re-energised talk of closer ties a decade after Britain voted to leave the European Union, and the mood was upbeat as the prime minister shook hands with EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa.

One potential dampener emerged as the 27-nation bloc and London jostled over linking ultimate implementation of the new deals to Britain agreeing to cut university fees for EU students -- but both sides cast the day as a win.

"This is a good day for Britain. This is a good day for Europe," Burnham told the gathering, hailing a "landmark" agreement -- while the EU's von der Leyen called it a "turning point" in relations.

Wrapped up in Brussels were three main agreements: a deal cutting red tape for food exports, another linking the two sides' emissions-trading schemes and a third on a "youth experience scheme".

Burnham argued the accords -- initiated by his predecessor, Keir Starmer -- will unpick some of the damage inflicted by the "hard Brexit we ended up with" and provide a US$22-billion boost to the British economy.

British firms will export to Europe more easily again and 100,000 under-30s from each side will be allowed to reside for up to three years in the other's territory for work, study or travel.

But while the optics at the meeting may have been much improved, old habits die hard.

Brussels and London wrangled down to the wire over the details of the deals.

One sticking point was on pinning London down to a future agreement on cutting fees for EU students at UK universities to the level paid by their British counterparts.

Burnham insisted that the "deal is done", even if talks would continue on tuition fees over the next six months.

But a statement from EU countries seen by AFP said they would hold off implementation until there was an agreement over the fees.

Since taking power this summer, Burnham has defied the taboos in Britain's toxic debate over Europe -- going as far as to float rejoining the bloc one day.

European Council boss Costa told Burnham the EU was open to having the "closest possible relationship".

But the summit focused on smaller steps, and the prime minister kicked the can on what could come next.

Having previously said he would like to see Britain rejoin the EU in his lifetime, Burnham has promised to lay out options that could range from leaving things as they are to entering the customs union or becoming a member again.

He said he would hold an "informal brainstorming" with the EU over the next year to look at options.

"We do need to consider what is the right long-term relationship. Incremental steps, as you say, only take us so far," Burnham said in response to a question from AFP -- while conceding Friday's deals were likely "the limit of what we can achieve in this parliament".

"The British people will be the boss of what happens next. We will not be running ahead of public opinion," he said.

Burnham hopes friendlier EU relations will help build a broad centre-left coalition to win the next general election, not anticipated until 2029.

Polls now regularly indicate most Britons regret Brexit.

However, Burnham's own party is divided on how to proceed.

The Labour leader's push leaves him open to accusations of Brexit betrayal from the opposition Conservatives and hard-right Reform UK party of Nigel Farage -- who shadowed Burnham to Brussels and delivered his own press conference.

"He's let the genie out of the bottle, and I think he's going to be very, very surprised by the backlash he gets," Farage told journalists. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Uber Parking could save you from circling the block
articles.excerpt: Uber Parking launches in 15 U.S. cities after the SpotHero deal, offering upfront prices, Uber One credits, and a future…
articles.fullText:
You finally make it downtown for dinner, but now comes the real challenge. Finding somewhere to park. You circle the block once, then again. Before you know it, you're late and getting frustrated. Sound familiar? Well, Uber thinks it has a solution. The company just launched Uber Parking, a new feature that lets you reserve a parking spot directly through the Uber app before you even leave home. Yes, the same company that built its business around getting you into someone else's car now wants to help when you drive your own. And there's another interesting twist. Uber has plans for those parking garages that involve robotaxis.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
UBER LETS PARENTS WATCH TEEN RIDES LIVE
On Nov. 9, Uber announced the launch of Uber Parking, bringing parking reservations directly into its app. The feature follows Uber's acquisition of SpotHero, a popular parking reservation service. Through that deal, Uber gained access to a network of more than 13,000 parking garages, lots and valet locations across more than 400 cities in the United States and Canada.
So, instead of driving around looking for parking, you can search for an available spot near your destination. You can also see the price upfront, making it easier to decide whether driving makes financial sense. For someone heading into the city for dinner or trying to get to an important appointment, that could save some aggravation. And if you've ever paid a small fortune to park somewhere, you'll probably appreciate being able to compare prices before arriving.
Uber has made the process pretty simple. You can book parking using the same app you already use to request a ride.
Here's how it works:
Once you've booked, your digital parking pass appears inside the Uber app. Depending on the location, you'll either scan a QR code or enter through a system that recognizes your license plate. Uber also says you can extend reservations through the app if you need more time. Cancellation policies vary by parking facility. Some reservations qualify for a full refund if canceled before the scheduled start time. Always check the booking terms before paying.
One thing worth mentioning: Uber generally won't physically park your car for you. Unless you choose a valet location, you'll still be the one behind the wheel.
FAKE E-ZPASS EMAIL THREATENS $100 FINE OVER UNPAID TOLL
Uber Parking launched in 15 U.S. cities on Nov. 9.
Those cities are:
Uber plans to expand the service into additional markets. However, there's an important detail here. Although SpotHero operates across more than 400 cities, Uber Parking has not yet expanded throughout that entire network. Also, the new feature is still rolling out. So, even if you're in one of the launch cities, you may not see the Parking icon immediately. First, make sure you're using the latest version of the Uber app. You can also visit SpotHero's website to search for parking in areas where the Uber feature is unavailable.
Here's a little bonus if you already pay for Uber One. Uber says eligible members can earn 10% back in Uber One credits on qualifying parking reservations once their parking session is complete. You can use those credits toward future eligible Uber rides or Uber Eats orders. For example, if you spend $30 on a qualifying parking reservation, you could earn $3 in Uber One credits.
That may not sound like a fortune. However, if you're regularly parking downtown, those credits could add up. Just keep in mind that the 10% reward only applies to eligible reservations. You also need an active Uber One membership to qualify and redeem the credits. And remember, these are Uber credits rather than cash back to your bank account. Before booking, compare the total parking price with other nearby options. A cheaper garage could still save you more money than the rewards you'd earn.
Uber also sees parking garages as part of its future robotaxi business . Think about it. When a driverless taxi drops someone off, what happens next? If another passenger needs a ride nearby, that's easy enough. But what happens when nobody needs the car? Does it keep driving around until another request comes in? That could mean more empty vehicles on already crowded streets. Uber is reportedly exploring ways to use parking facilities as waiting areas for autonomous vehicles. Instead of driving around without passengers, robotaxis could pull into nearby garages and wait for their next assignment.
Then, when someone requests a ride, the vehicle could head out to pick them up. Uber believes that approach could reduce unnecessary driving and help lower operating costs. There's another potential benefit. Keeping autonomous vehicles in nearby facilities could make it easier to have them ready when demand increases. However, this remains a developing plan. Uber has not announced that every SpotHero garage will accommodate robotaxis, and the company has not provided a timeline for a broad rollout of these facilities. For now, the immediate focus remains helping people find parking for their own cars.
There's something else worth paying attention to here. For years, Uber built its business around giving people an alternative to driving. Now, the company wants you opening its app even when you plan to take your own car. Let's say you're going downtown for dinner. You could check the price of an Uber ride. Then, you could compare that with the cost of driving and parking.
If driving looks cheaper, you can reserve a space through Uber. If taking a ride makes more sense, you can book that instead. Either way, Uber stays part of your plans. And as autonomous vehicles become more common, the company could eventually use that same parking network to support its robotaxi partners. It's an interesting strategy, especially as Uber looks for more ways to keep people using its app.
The biggest benefit is pretty straightforward. You may be able to reserve parking before leaving home and spend less time driving around looking for an available spot. That could be especially useful when you're heading somewhere unfamiliar or trying to make a flight. However, there are a few things I'd recommend checking before you book.
Don't assume Uber offers the lowest rate. Check the final price against other parking options before paying. Also, make sure your reservation covers the time you'll actually need.
Some parking garages have height limits. If you drive a larger SUV or truck, check those restrictions before booking. Also, confirm the exact entrance address, which may differ from the garage's street address.
Some parking reservations can be canceled for free before they begin, but the rules vary by location. Review the specific garage's cancellation terms before booking. Once your reservation starts, Uber says it can no longer be canceled or refunded.
Some garages use QR codes for entry. That's convenient, but criminals have also placed fake QR codes on parking meters to trick drivers into visiting fraudulent payment websites. Use the parking pass provided directly through your Uber app rather than scanning an unfamiliar sticker. We've previously reported on how criminals use fake parking QR codes to steal money.
Even with a reservation, finding your car afterward can still be a headache. Fortunately, Google Maps and Apple Maps have tools that can help you remember where you parked. Our guide to finding your parked car with Maps explains how to set them up.
I think Uber is onto something here. Who hasn't wasted time driving around looking for parking, especially when you're already running late? Being able to reserve a spot before leaving home sounds pretty convenient. Of course, I'd want to make sure I'm getting a good price. But what really caught my attention is Uber's plan to use parking garages for robotaxis. Having driverless cars park between rides makes sense, especially if it means fewer empty vehicles clogging up our streets. Still, I wonder what happens when those garages start filling up with robotaxis. Will there be enough room for the rest of us? That's something I'll be watching as this technology takes off.
Would you trust Uber to handle your parking reservations, or do you worry that parking garages could eventually become crowded with robotaxis, leaving fewer spaces for the rest of us? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

articles.title: AIIB office agreement signed
articles.excerpt: The Government of the People's Republic of China and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) today signed an agreement, in…
articles.fullText:
The Government of the People's Republic of China and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) today signed an agreement, in Hong Kong, that lays the foundation for the AIIB to set up an office in the city.

The agreement was signed by Minister of Finance Lan Fo'an and AIIB President Ms Zou Jiayi. It confirms that an AIIB office will be established in Hong Kong, and sets out principles for its establishment, along with other matters.

Speaking at the signing ceremony, Financial Secretary Paul Chan said the AIIB's decision to establish an office in Hong Kong is a clear recognition of the city's status as an international financial centre, and underscores the city's unique role in pooling international capital and supporting infrastructure development in Asia. He stressed that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government will render its full support for the office.

“We look forward to strengthening co-operation with the AIIB, so that Hong Kong's capital market and professional services can provide greater support for its business development and mobilise more international capital for infrastructure investment and financing in Asia."

Mr Chan added that, in line with its established practice of facilitating the operations of international organisations in Hong Kong, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government will introduce subsidiary legislation in the Legislative Council as soon as possible to formally confer necessary privileges and immunities on the AIIB's Hong Kong office.

In addition, Acting Secretary for Financial Services & the Treasury Joseph Chan signed an agreement on behalf of the Hong Kong SAR Government with the AIIB's Chief Partnerships Officer Hun Kim, to contribute US$20 million to the "Project Preparation Special Fund" to enable the establishment of the AIIB's office in Hong Kong.

articles.title: Election arrangements inspected
articles.excerpt: Ahead of tomorrow's 2026 Election Committee Subsector Ordinary Elections, Chairman of the Electoral Affairs Commission David Lok visited the polling…
articles.fullText:
Ahead of tomorrow's 2026 Election Committee Subsector Ordinary Elections, Chairman of the Electoral Affairs Commission David Lok visited the polling station at Harbour Road Sports Centre, and the Central Counting Station (CCS) at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre (HKCEC) this morning, and appealed to eligible voters to cast their votes in the poll.

He said that preparatory work for the elections was complete and that staff were carrying out final rehearsals. He thanked them for their efforts to ensure that tomorrow’s poll is conducted openly, honestly and fairly.

A total of 856 candidates are contesting 723 seats in 31 subsectors.

Five ordinary polling stations (OPSs) will be open from 9am to 6pm for voters or authorised representatives (ARs) in the relevant subsectors to cast their votes. Voters and ARs are reminded to bring their original, valid Hong Kong identity cards to vote at the polling station specified on their poll card.

Mr Justice Lok highlighted that the Electronic Poll Register System will be used at OPSs to issuing ballot papers to voters or ARs.

Once the poll is closed, all ballot boxes will be delivered to the CCS, where counting of votes will take place. Candidates, election agents and counting agents will be able to enter the CCS and observe the count at designated areas of the counting zone. Members of the public and the media will be able to enter the public area of the CCS to observe the count.

This afternoon, Mr Lok and Secretary for Constitutional & Mainland Affairs Janice Tse Siu-wa accompanied Chief Executive John Lee on a visit to the polling station at the Harbour Road Sports Centre to observe final preparatory work being undertaken.

The EAC and the Registration & Electoral Office said they are fully prepared on all fronts to ensure that the elections are conducted smoothly and in a fair, impartial, honest and safe manner.

articles.title: Sports dispute summit to be held
articles.excerpt: The Department of Justice (DoJ), the Law Society of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Bar Association will co-host the…
articles.fullText:
The Department of Justice (DoJ), the Law Society of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Bar Association will co-host the Sports Dispute Resolution Summit on December 1.

Showcasing Hong Kong's unique strengths and potential in the field, the summit will deepen the city's position as an international legal and dispute resolution services centre.

It will bring together leading experts in sports law and dispute resolution from around the world, including representatives from the Court of Arbitration for Sport, the French National Bar Council (Conseil national des barreaux), the China Commission of Arbitration for Sport, and Hong Kong's legal professional bodies.

Deputy Secretary for Justice and Chairperson of the Advisory Committee on Sports Dispute Resolution Cheung Kwok-kwan outlined that the DoJ has been working closely with Hong Kong's sports and legal sectors to explore collaboration with international and regional sports organisations, with a view to promoting the city's sports dispute resolution services globally.

Following the establishment of the Advisory Committee on Sports Dispute Resolution early last year and the launch of a two-year Pilot Scheme on Sports Dispute Resolution last December, a positive response has been received from the community, he said.

He highlighted that with the opening of the Kai Tak Sports Park and the successive staging of major international sports events in Hong Kong, the local sports industry is developing at full speed. Establishing a fair and efficient dispute resolution mechanism has therefore become indispensable, he added.

Mr Cheung said that, in leveraging the unique advantages of the "one country, two systems" framework, a robust common law system, world-class dispute resolution institutions and professionals, as well as the synergy arising from hosting the International Organization for Mediation, Hong Kong is ideally placed to become an international sports dispute resolution centre.

The Government is also striving to attract major international sports organisations to establish a presence in Hong Kong, he said, revealing that the headquarters of a major regional sports law organisation will be set up in the city imminently.

Featuring two panel discussions, the summit will explore the latest trends and future developments in international sports mediation and arbitration from diverse perspectives spanning the Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Asia and the international community.

The summit will be held from 9.30am to 1pm on December 1. Registration is free and open online now.

articles.title: Global praise for HK infrastructure
articles.excerpt: InfraEX Week 2026 opened yesterday with its flagship event – the 2nd International Infrastructure and Projects Leaders Summit – bringing…
articles.fullText:
InfraEX Week 2026 opened yesterday with its flagship event – the 2nd International Infrastructure and Projects Leaders Summit – bringing together leading experts and professionals from over 30 countries and regions.

Participants praised the summit’s strong global appeal and shared positive views on Hong Kong’s ongoing infrastructure development.

Ashghal Technical Office Assistant Manager Hayat Bukshaisha said that Hong Kong has strong experience in planning and delivering major infrastructure projects.

“We are taking Hong Kong as a benchmark. We look to Hong Kong and learn from past experience, especially when it comes to modern methods of construction and project delivery,” she said.

Deloitte Australia Senior Partner Sean McClowry noted that he is particularly interested in the Northern Metropolis Project.

“It is one of the most exciting initiatives of its kind in the world, and seeing this kind of greenfield initiative coming to life is really exciting for me,” he said. “Always when I come to Hong Kong, just seeing how the infrastructure works together and how you fuse physical infrastructure and digital technologies is very interesting to me.”

Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Singapore Executive Director (Centre for Public Project Management) Low Chian Siong highlighted the value of opportunities that he gained by joining the event.

“The greatest takeaway for me is not just learning what other participants are doing, but also actually the network that we create and continue to maintain,” he said.

He said he was also amazed by how much Hong Kong has achieved in a very short time in terms of planning and execution.

Meanwhile, Professor Tarek Zayed of The Hong Kong Polytechnic University Department of Construction Management & Intelligence, who has spent nine years working in Hong Kong, emphasised the city’s high standards in infrastructure.

“I have been in contact with many departments in Hong Kong and doing a lot of research in many infrastructures including bridges, tunnels, water networks, sewer networks, highways or pavement. The infrastructure here is strong, very good, and many of them are new, very sustainable and resilient for the coming generation.”

Association of Consulting Engineers of Hong Kong Chairman Ole Wong said that the summit encourages valuable exchanges with overseas professionals.

“We can share, we can collaborate and we think about an integrated opportunity with each other together. So the summit is very successful and we hope we can meet as many leaders as possible from different places. We can all work together and we can think about our future, embrace our challenges together,” he said.

articles.title: How a temple on a rock became a monument
articles.excerpt: Wan Chai’s Queen’s Road East is a bustling thoroughfare lined with towering skyscrapers, yet sitting quietly in a corner of…
articles.fullText:
Wan Chai’s Queen’s Road East is a bustling thoroughfare lined with towering skyscrapers, yet sitting quietly in a corner of this urban hub is a historic temple. Built between 1847 and 1852, Hung Shing Temple has endured for nearly 180 years and was officially declared a monument by the Government in October 2026.

Shifting shorelines
Dedicated to Hung Shing, the God of the South Sea widely worshipped by fishermen and merchant seafarers, the temple has deep maritime roots – making its current inland setting seem puzzling at first glance.

Development Bureau Antiquities & Monuments Office Curator (Historic Buildings) Alice Yu explained the mystery: “Hung Shing Temple was originally built on the shoreline of Hong Kong Island. The two streets opposite the temple – Tai Wong Street East and Tai Wong Street West – are both named after the temple's popular name, Tai Wong.”

Through decades of land reclamation and urban development, the sea that once stretched before the temple has given way to busy streets and high-rises. Today, the temple serves as a historical landmark, silently chronicling Wan Chai’s shifting coastline.

Lingnan craftsmanship
Beyond its historical significance, Hung Shing Temple stands out as an architectural gem in the Lingnan style. It features a traditional single-hall, three-bay layout, complete with an elevated entrance porch and an unusual side-access design.

Exquisite granite columns carved with human figures and "prawn-shaped" tie beams support the porch, while granite balustrades – centred around an intricate double-dragon-and-pearl motif – frame the entrance. Crowning the roof are ornate Shiwan ridge decorations from 1909, depicting the legendary heroine Fan Lihua.

Stepping inside reveals the building's most astonishing architectural feature: the temple was built directly onto a natural rock formation. Ms Yu noted that the rock merges seamlessly with the structure, becoming part of the temple itself.

“This kind of structure, which adapts to the terrain and features a coexistence between the temple and the rock formation, is quite rare among temples in Hong Kong,” she said. “The temple walls had to follow the uneven and irregular surface of the rock, demonstrating the craftsmanship and architectural wisdom of tailoring (a structure) to local conditions.”

Shared devotion
That the temple has survived in remarkably original condition for nearly two centuries is a testament to the dedicated care of generations of local residents and caretakers. Following major expansions and upgrades in 1860 and 1867 – heavily backed by the Chinese community and a local quarry firm – the temple flourished.

In the past, worshippers placed ancestral soul tablets inside the temple. Over time, it gradually welcomed a variety of deities, including Lady Kam Fa for safe childbirth and Lady Fa Fan for eternal youth, as well as Man Cheong, Wah To and Tai Sui – reflecting the inclusive, multi-deity nature of Chinese folk beliefs.

Living heritage
In the face of changing times, the temple’s management has introduced fresh initiatives in recent years to connect traditional heritage with younger generations. Tung Wah Group of Hospitals Senior Manager (Temple & Cultural Services) Vandesar Leung noted that while preserving traditional worship services, the organisation is committed to hosting events, as well as developing cultural and creative products.

“We aim to attract more citizens and visitors to discover Hung Shing Temple through guided tours, education programmes and cultural promotion. By offering workshops and lectures, and including the temple in tour routes, we highlight how Hung Shing worship connects with fishing village history and Wan Chai’s growth.”

“More than a historic building, the temple is a living cultural witness,” he said.

From a modest shrine on a bygone shoreline to a declared monument in the heart of a modern metropolis, Hung Shing Temple in Wan Chai does more than record a community's faith and transformation. It stands as a living bridge between past and future – safeguarding the historical memory of this city.

articles.title: FS to visit UK and Netherlands
articles.excerpt: Financial Secretary Paul Chan will depart for a visit to the United Kingdom and the Netherlands late tonight. He will…
articles.fullText:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan will depart for a visit to the United Kingdom and the Netherlands late tonight.

He will lead a delegation of over 20 members, comprising representatives of various government departments, public organisations and industry bodies, as well as leaders from the investment and innovation and technology (I&T) sectors, to enhance business and I&T exchanges between Hong Kong and the two places, promote opportunites in Hong Kong, and foster investment and collaboration.

During their visit to the UK from November 22 to 25, the delegation will visit the University of Cambridge and attend a dialogue on innovation co-organised by the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC) and the university.

They will also visit the university's innovation commercialisation arm and the research and development centre of a biopharmaceutical company. In London, they will attend the plenary session of the Hong Kong-Europe Business Council, a lunch hosted by the Hong Kong Association, and a Hong Kong Dinner organised by the HKTDC.

Mr Chan will also meet with local business, financial and think tank leaders, and attend a financial sector roundtable while in the UK capital.

During their visit to the Netherlands from November 25 to 28, the delegation will stop in Amsterdam, The Hague and Eindhoven to visit various I&T companies, parks and hubs. They will also participate in a number of business lunches to brief various sectors of the local community on developments in Hong Kong.

In addition, Mr Chan will meet local political, business, financial and think tank leaders, and attend a number of roundtable meetings and exchange sessions.

He will arrive back in Hong Kong on the morning of November 29. During his absence, Deputy Financial Secretary Michael Wong will be Acting Financial Secretary.

articles.title: Spain, France to clash in Nations League quarter-final
articles.excerpt: World champions Spain will face France, while England will play Norway in the quarter-finals of the Uefa Nations League, after…
articles.fullText:
World champions Spain will face France, while England will play Norway in the quarter-finals of the Uefa Nations League, after the draw took place on Friday.

Spain beat France 2-0 in the semi-finals of the World Cup in the United States in July, on the way to winning the trophy. They also defeated Les Bleus 5-4 in the semi-finals of the last edition of the Nations League, last year.

"This will not be about getting revenge for the World Cup semi-final," Zinedine Zidane, who was appointed France coach following that tournament, told L'Equipe.

"We knew we were going to get a strong opponent and we have got the reigning world champions."

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs in late March, with Spain at home first after coming second in Group A3, while France topped Group A1.

Spain won the Nations League in 2023, while France beat them to win the 2021 final.

England topped Group A3 on goal difference after beating Spain away in their last outing, and their reward is a two-legged last-eight tie against Norway with the first leg on Norwegian soil.

England edged Norway in the World Cup quarter-finals this year before losing to Argentina in the semi-finals.

The other quarter-final ties pitched reigning Nations League champions Portugal against the Netherlands, and Belgium against Germany.

"So much can happen in the time between now and then," Germany coach Jurgen Klopp told the German team's in-house broadcaster, DFB TV.

"We're very happy with the last impression we left, but we're also fully aware that we are right at the beginning of a development process," added Klopp, whose team topped Group A2 after thrashing the Netherlands 5-0 in Berlin on Monday.

"We want to carry this positive momentum forward. There's still a great deal of work to be done."

The winners of the quarter-finals will advance to the final stages, which will be held in June in a venue yet to be decided.

Spain or France will play the Netherlands or Portugal in the semis, with England facing Belgium or Germany should they get past Norway.

The Nations League quarter-finals and play-offs in March will all take place at the same time as qualifying begins for Euro 2028. (AFP)

Edited by Raymond Yeung

articles.title: COP31 deal elusive as fossil fuel fight deepens
articles.excerpt: The UN's COP31 climate talks were set to spill into overtime on Friday as countries remained deadlocked over a draft…
articles.fullText:
The UN's COP31 climate talks were set to spill into overtime on Friday as countries remained deadlocked over a draft deal that makes no mention of fossil fuels, with a host of other disputes also snarling negotiations.

Grey skies added to the sombre mood in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya as negotiators from nearly 200 countries struggled to bridge their differences after two weeks of intense talks, which could now run into the weekend.

"At this point, no one is happy," Brazil's national secretary for climate change, Aloisio Lopes Pereira de Melo, told reporters with only hours before the conference's official end.

The talks come with a series of stark reminders of the urgency of climate action, from heatwaves in Europe and devastating floods in Nepal, while a record-breaking El Nino – a periodic warming pattern – supercharges temperatures.

But expectations for a major breakthrough are low at COP31 as countries cope with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran.

A sprawling initial draft deal earlier this week called for accelerating the phase-out of fossil fuels, along with other flashpoint topics such as finance and climate science.

But a new, shorter version released by COP31 co-host Australia on Thursday omitted any mention of the main drivers of climate change, sparking calls for the language to be restored.

Instead, the draft "cover decision" calls for electrifying the world economy, saying it could have "significant benefits" in shoring up energy security and cutting planet-heating greenhouse gas emissions.

The text reflects a push by COP31 host Türkiye for countries to rally behind a goal to increase the global share of final energy demand met by electricity to 35 percent by 2035.

But some countries want the text to call for "clean" electrification to make clear that renewables, not coal or gas, must be the energy source.

Nations agreed at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 to transition away from fossil fuels, without setting targets or timelines, but Saudi Arabia and other major oil producers have fiercely resisted any attempt to bring the issue back to the table.

A dozen European and developing countries – from France to Panama and the Solomon Islands – released a letter insisting that the text include "a clear transition away from fossil fuels".

Panama's environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, said "the COP can still be saved" if the deal includes the phase-out and other issues, including a defence of climate science.

An outspoken critic of what he calls the "petroleum mafia", Navarro has threatened to block any deal that does not include a cap on oil production.

A European Union official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP that the latest draft was "not acceptable and not ambitious enough".

"We don't want this COP to become a 'fossil' COP," the official said.

Countries are sharply divided over a raft of other issues.

A fight over the timing of the next set of reports by the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has been a major source of friction.

The draft also expresses "deep concern" about the imminent breach of the 1.5-degree Celsius goal set under the 2015 Paris accord.

Negotiations are also deadlocked over long-running complaints by developing countries that rich nations are falling short in their obligations to help them confront climate change.

"We didn't come here to beg," said Ghana's environment minister, Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings.

"The (African) continent will not accept an outcome that offers declarations without the resources to deliver them," she said. (AFP)

Edited by Raymond Yeung

articles.title: Hackers use Microsoft Outlook security flaw to steal your login data
articles.excerpt: Microsoft Outlook flaw CVE-2026-124194 lets a malicious .msg file expose NTLMv2 authentication data, and Microsoft confirms hackers already exploited it.
articles.fullText:
You probably know better than to enter your password on a suspicious website. But what if hackers could steal information tied to your Windows login without ever asking for your password? That's the concern behind a Microsoft Outlook security flaw that hackers are already exploiting. Attackers can trick someone into opening a malicious Outlook file that quietly exposes Windows authentication information. That information could help a criminal impersonate you and potentially gain access to systems you use.
Microsoft released a fix on Nov. 10. However, the company confirms hackers were exploiting the vulnerability before the update became available. If you use Outlook for work, this is one security update you should check right away.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
FAKE AI EVENT INVITES TARGET MICROSOFT AND GOOGLE LOGINS
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-124194, involves how Outlook handles specially crafted message files. An attacker can create a malicious Outlook message file, such as one using the .msg format. The hacker then needs to convince someone to open that file in an affected version of Outlook. Once opened, the malicious file can cause Outlook to connect to a server controlled by the attacker. That connection happens without the usual warning about accessing external content. During the connection, Windows can reveal NTLMv2 authentication information . This data helps Windows verify your identity when connecting to certain network services.
The information differs from your actual password. However, hackers may be able to use it in a follow-up attack to impersonate you. For someone using Outlook at work, that could potentially expose company resources their account can access. The outcome depends on the network's security protections and whether the attacker can successfully misuse the authentication information. Here's what makes this especially concerning. The attack doesn't require you to type your password into a fake login page. Opening the malicious file can be enough if your computer can connect to the attacker's network location. Microsoft says simply viewing the message through Outlook's Preview Pane does not trigger this particular vulnerability. Someone must open the malicious file for the attack to work.
Microsoft included the Outlook fix in its November Patch Tuesday security updates. The company's core release addressed 1,093 vulnerabilities, including 63 rated critical. Interestingly, Microsoft classified this particular Outlook vulnerability as moderate, giving it a CVSS severity score of 6.5 out of 10. However, that rating tells only part of the story. Microsoft confirms attackers have already exploited the flaw. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) also added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Nov. 10. In other words, hackers are already taking advantage of this security weakness. Microsoft has not publicly identified who carried out the attacks or disclosed how many people were affected. The company also hasn't provided detailed information about the incidents. With hackers already exploiting the flaw, it's important to install the security update as soon as possible.
FAKE CHATGPT BILLING EMAILS CAN STEAL YOUR LOGIN
According to Microsoft's security advisory, the affected products include:
The vulnerability concerns affected desktop Office installations on Windows computers. Microsoft's advisory does not list Outlook.com in a web browser or the Outlook mobile apps as affected products. If your employer manages your Microsoft 365 software, your IT department may handle these updates. However, it's worth confirming that the security fix has been installed. For people who manage their own computers, here's how to check.
The most important thing you can do is update Microsoft Office. However, a few additional precautions can help reduce your exposure to suspicious files and account attacks.
Microsoft has released security updates addressing the vulnerability. You can manually check for updates in supported Windows versions of Office.
If you don't see Update Now, you may need to select Enable Updates first. If the entire Update Options menu is missing, your employer may manage updates centrally. Contact your IT department rather than assuming the software has already been patched. You can also review Microsoft's official Office update instructions.
After installing the update, you can check which version of Office is running on your computer.
For affected volume-licensed installations, Microsoft's November 10 security release includes these updated builds:
These build numbers apply to the specified LTSC editions. They shouldn't be used to check other Office versions. If you're using Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise, the correct build depends on your organization's update channel. You can check Microsoft's Office security release notes or contact your IT department to confirm the fix.
Although this vulnerability requires an Office fix, keeping Windows updated remains important.
On Windows 11:
Next, check whether Windows can receive updates for other Microsoft products.
This can help Windows deliver updates for supported Microsoft products. However, some Office installations receive updates through separate services or employer-managed systems. Remember that checking Windows Update alone may not confirm you've installed the specific Outlook fix. Check Office separately. It's also smart to back up important files before installing major operating system updates.
A message file from an unfamiliar sender deserves extra caution, especially if you weren't expecting it. Watch for attachments ending in .msg, a common file format for saved Outlook messages. The format itself is legitimate. However, attackers can abuse it to deliver this exploit. If an email claims you need to open an attached message to review an invoice or urgent workplace request, verify it through another trusted channel. Even attachments appearing to come from coworkers deserve a second look when the request seems unusual.
If something looks suspicious, avoid opening the attachment. Instead, report the message using Outlook's built-in reporting tools when available.
In supported versions of Outlook:
The exact menu location depends on your Outlook version and your employer's settings. If you're using a work account and don't see a reporting option, contact your IT department. Avoid forwarding the suspicious attachment to other coworkers.
Strong antivirus software can help identify suspicious attachments and malicious activity before they cause further damage. Look for protection that includes real-time scanning and behavior-based detection. These features may help catch threats that traditional virus signatures miss. However, antivirus software cannot replace Microsoft's security patch. Installing the Outlook update remains essential for closing this particular vulnerability. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.
Multifactor authentication (MFA) adds another layer of account protection by requiring additional verification when you sign in. Enable it on your Microsoft account and other important services whenever available. Keep in mind that MFA may not stop attacks involving stolen Windows authentication information. That's another reason updating Outlook takes priority.
If you recently opened an unexpected Outlook message attachment, don't assume everything is fine because nothing unusual appeared on your screen. Here's what to do next.
One important reminder: Changing your password alone may not address every potential exposure from this vulnerability. If you opened the attachment on a work computer, let your IT team determine whether additional security measures are necessary.
Microsoft's November security release covers far more than Outlook. It also fixes weaknesses that could allow attackers to gain additional privileges or remotely execute malicious code. For those of you using a Windows PC every day, the sheer number of vulnerabilities may sound overwhelming. However, not every flaw carries the same immediate risk. In this case, the Outlook weakness deserves your attention because Microsoft has confirmed active exploitation.
The larger concern is how easily a malicious file can take advantage of trusted software. Outlook is part of everyday communication for countless businesses, and opening saved email messages may seem harmless. This vulnerability shows why keeping Office updated deserves the same attention as updating Windows.
What concerns me about this Outlook flaw is how little someone has to do to put their information at risk. You could receive what looks like a routine work attachment, open it and unknowingly expose information that helps a hacker impersonate you. There's no obvious warning telling you something went wrong. And by the time you realize it, the damage may already be done. I also find it troubling that Microsoft rated this vulnerability moderate even though attackers were already exploiting it. Most people aren't going to spend their day reviewing security ratings, and they shouldn't have to. They need software that protects them and updates that are easy to install. My advice is simple. If you use Outlook on a Windows computer, check for Office updates today. Don't assume your computer has already taken care of it.
Should Microsoft be doing more to prevent a single malicious Outlook file from exposing your login information, or do you think keeping your software updated is enough protection? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

articles.title: Top seed Wang Zhiyi through to HK Badminton Open semis
articles.excerpt: China's top seed Wang Zhiyi advanced to the women's singles semifinals at the Hong Kong Open Badminton Championships 2026 on…
articles.fullText:
China's top seed Wang Zhiyi advanced to the women's singles semifinals at the Hong Kong Open Badminton Championships 2026 on Friday, while men's doubles stars Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang bowed out in the quarterfinals.

Wang edged sixth seed Putri Kusuma Wardani of Indonesia 22-20, 22-20 in a tightly contested match.

After clinching a close opening game, Wang led 18-15 in the second before Wardani reeled off five straight points to reach game point. Keeping her composure under pressure, the Chinese shuttler responded with four consecutive points to seal the victory in straight games.

"When I dropped five points in a row and fell behind in the second game, I told myself to stay calm and focused, and make adjustments," Wang said.

In the men's doubles, Liang and Wang, silver medalists at the 2024 Paris Olympics, fell to South Korean duo Kang Min-hyuk and Lee Jong-min 19-21, 21-19, 18-21.

Fellow Chinese pair Hu Keyuan and Lin Xiangyi also exited the tournament, losing 2-1 to Hangzhou Asian Games champions Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty of India.

In mixed doubles, top seeds Feng Yanzhe and Huang Dongping needed just 26 minutes to eliminate Chinese Taipei's Wu Hsuan-yi and Yang Chu-yun in straight games.

"We prepared thoroughly for a tough battle and executed our game plan well, preventing our opponents from finding any way to restrict us," Huang said.

Second seeds Jiang Zhenbang and Wei Yaxin also cruised into the mixed doubles semifinals.

The Hong Kong Open is part of the BWF World Tour Super 500 and runs from November 17 to 22. (Xinhua)

articles.title: Govt going all out to help Wang Fuk residents: CS
articles.excerpt: The government is doing everything it can to help residents of Wang Fuk Court to move on and start a…
articles.fullText:
The government is doing everything it can to help residents of Wang Fuk Court to move on and start a new life, Chief Secretary Eric Chan said on Friday.

Ahead of the one-year anniversary of the fire that killed 168 people at the Tai Po housing estate, Chan stressed that the public can freely attend memorial events so long as they are legal.

Responding to reporters' questions after officiating at the opening ceremony of a Community Living Room in North Point, Chan said he had heard that certain groups were being pressured to cancel certain memorial activities.

"I would like to clarify here and reiterate that Hong Kong is governed by the rule of law. Any memorial activities, as long as they are legal, are absolutely permitted by the government," he said, citing examples such as events held by religious bodies.

But he urged the public to be careful in choosing which events to attend, saying there are individuals with ulterior motives who wish to use this opportunity to create trouble.

"I want to remind our citizens that when participating in such memorial events, they must be careful in their choices and make sure not to be taken advantage of by people with hidden agendas," he said.

If in doubt, Chan suggested the public enquire with the government.

The chief secretary said that the government, led by Chief Executive John Lee, had been going all out to assist residents affected by the fire, including rehousing them as soon as possible.

But most importantly, he said, is how reforms must be implemented to prevent a repeat of the disaster, citing ongoing legislative amendments to minimise fire risks and stamp out bid-rigging in building maintenance projects.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Hong Kong inflation remains moderate at 2.2pc
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong's consumer inflation remained moderate in October, with overall prices rising by 2.2 percent year on year. The figure…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong's consumer inflation remained moderate in October, with overall prices rising by 2.2 percent year on year.

The figure, published by the Census and Statistics Department on Friday, compared with the 1.9 percent expansion in September, although the government attributed the larger increase last month to the end of the rates concession.

For the first 10 months of 2026, the composite consumer price index (CPI) rose by 1.8 percent over the same period a year ago.

Netting out the effects of the government's one-off relief measures, the underlying inflation in October stood at two percent, compared to 2.1 percent in September.

Breaking down the various components of the composite CPI, prices jumped by 12.7 percent for electricity, gas and water and 11.4 percent for health services.

Transport costs, which are sensitive to rising fuel prices, increased by 4.5 percent.

There were milder increases for necessities such as food, which edged up by 0.3 percent, while housing rents ticked up 1.4 percent.

A government spokesman noted that the prices of fuel-related items continued to rise noticeably.

"But spillover effects remained limited, with prices of most other items increasing modestly or declining," he said.

Looking ahead, the spokesman said price pressures on other fronts should remain broadly in check, although geopolitical tensions remain a key source of near-term uncertainty for international fuel prices.

Edited by Tony Sabine

Mainland and Hong Kong stocks ended sharply lower on Friday, with tech shares leading losses after a steep Wall Street selloff weighed on investor sentiment, while Anthropic's much-anticipated IPO did little to revive waning optimism surrounding the artificial intelligence sector.

The benchmark Hang Seng Index ended 430 points, or 1.9 percent, lower at 22,410 on turnover of HK$270.3 billion.

The tech index dived 138 points, or 3.8 percent, to 3,511 while the China enterprises index was 135 points, or 1.8 percent, down at 7,554.

Up north, the Shanghai Composite Index closed down 43 points, or 1.22 percent, at 3,533 on turnover of 702.57 billion yuan while the blue-chip CSI300 index lost 0.8 percent.

Both indexes recorded their lowest closing levels since July 2025.

For the week, the Shanghai Composite fell 2.8 percent to notch the biggest weekly drop since July, and the CSI300 lost 1.5 percent.

Investor sentiment was also weighed down by signs that Washington is tightening tech curbs on China, despite meetings between the leaders of the world's two largest economies this week.

The Shenzhen Component Index closed down 326 points, or 3.09 percent, at 10,256 on turnover of 719.62 billion yuan while the ChiNext Index closed down 81 points, or 3.54 percent, at 2,212 on turnover of 334.97 billion yuan.

The decline came after US stocks slumped on Thursday, as AI-related shares came under pressure following Anthropic's much-anticipated IPO's failure to sustain an early rally.

"The optimism failed to lift the broader AI sector, as concerns over stretched valuations and elevated capex spending continued to weigh on sentiment," analysts at OCBC said in a note.

In China, tech sectors that require huge computing power, such as big data, AI and cloud computing all fell sharply.

Hong Kong-listed shares of Chinese AI model developers, which rely heavily on advanced computing power, also tumbled.

Minimax slumped 10.8 percent to record lows, bringing this week's loss to more than 30 percent.

Z.AI shares declined 7.2 percent, bringing the weekly loss to 18.2 percent.

Semiconductor shares were among the biggest drags, with a subindex tracking the sector plunging 3.9 percent.

Sentiment towards chipmakers was also hurt by TSMC tightening restrictions on Chinese chip designers, suspending some previously permitted advanced manufacturing orders and generally limiting affected customers to older chipmaking technology, sources said.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei ended 3,007 points, or 5.06 percent, at 56,436 amid chip and tech related plunges of 10.32 percent for Advantest, 7.06 percent for Tokyo Electron, 14.48 percent for technology investor SoftBank Group and 11.66 percent for memory chip maker Kioxia.

For the week, the index lost 7.7 percent.

The broader Topix fell 148 points, or 3.88 percent, to 3,674 for the day.

In Seoul, the Kospi closed down 267 points, or 5.21 percent, at 4,869 as chipmaker losses of 7.01 percent piled up for Samsung Electronics and 5.92 percent for SK Hynix. (Agencies)
