articles.title: World Court finds Myanmar responsible for Rohingya genocide in landmark ruling
articles.excerpt: Experts say the judgment marks a historic victory for the Rohingya but enforcement remains a challenge.
articles.fullText:
Updated on Nov. 19, 2026 at 11:21 a.m. ET
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled on Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, in a landmark judgment that could increase diplomatic pressure on its military-led government.
In a 9-6 decision, the United Nations’ top court found that Myanmar had violated the 1948 Genocide Convention during a military crackdown that drove more than 730,000 Rohingya to neighboring Bangladesh in 2017.
It was the first time the court had found a state responsible for committing genocide.
The judgment comes as Myanmar’s President Min Aung Hlaing, who commanded the military during the crackdown, seeks to restore his country’s international standing.
“This is a historic ruling. For the first time, the world court has found a state responsible for committing genocide – and the man who commanded those operations is now Myanmar’s president,” Richard Horsey, senior adviser for Asia at the Belgium-based International Crisis Group, said in a statement.
“The Rohingya have waited nine years to hear a court say this. It will not change their lives quickly, but it puts what was done to them on the legal record, and no amount of denial in Naypyidaw can remove it.”
UN top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said evidence showed that Myanmar’s security forces had killed some 10,000 Rohingya during the crackdown.
“The Court finds that Myanmar’s security forces killed thousands of Rohingya ⁠civilians, perpetrated widespread acts ⁠of sexual violence as well as acts of ⁠extreme violence against children and ⁠attacked fleeing Rohingya ⁠as they sought to flee in large numbers to ‌Bangladesh,” Iwasawa said.
The court concluded that the only reasonable inference from the evidence was that Myanmar’s security forces intended to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population.
It also found that Myanmar had failed to fulfill its obligation to prevent genocide.
The case was brought in 2019 by The Gambia, which accused Myanmar of violating the Genocide Convention and sought to hold the Southeast Asian nation accountable for atrocities against the predominantly Muslim ethnic minority.
Myanmar has maintained that its military operations were in response to attacks on police posts by the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, a Rohingya armed group.
Diplomatic pressure
While the judgment establishes Myanmar’s legal responsibility for genocide, questions remain over its practical consequences and whether other governments will reconsider their engagement with Naypyitaw.
“Governments rolling out the red carpet for Min Aung Hlaing will now be doing so for the head of a state found responsible for genocide. Most will carry on regardless, but it will be harder to present this as business as usual,” Horsey said.
“The court has no means of enforcing this ruling. What matters now is whether the governments engaging Naypyitaw are prepared to attach any cost to ignoring it.”
Myanmar's Union Minister for the Ministry of the President's Office Ko Ko Hlaing attends a hearing on the day the International Court of Justice delivers its judgment in the case brought by Gambia accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority, in The Hague, Netherlands, Nov. 19, 2026.
(Piroschka Van De Wouw/Reuters) Horsey added that the ruling was likely to make Myanmar’s government more defensive in its dealings with the United Nations as it sought to regain its seat at the world body.
Human rights advocates called on governments to use the judgment to press Myanmar to end abuses against the Rohingya.
“The International Court of Justice’s landmark ruling is long-awaited recognition of the suffering the Rohingya have endured from Myanmar’s military. The ruling also provides a significant precedent for victims of genocide, and other grave crimes, across the world in their own quest for justice,” Maria Elena Vignoli, senior international justice counsel at New York-based Human Rights Watch, said in a statement.
In response to the ruling, the United Kingdom will order the expulsion of the Myanmar defense attaché and call on the U.N. Security Council to address it, the UK’s foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, said in a statement.
“The Rohingya have endured years of appalling violence, displacement and persecution.” Miliband said. “Myanmar must comply fully with the judgement. The international community must now play its part in supporting implementation, accountability, and justice for the Rohingya.”
Uncertain future for refugees
The ruling comes amid a humanitarian crisis compounded by renewed fighting in Myanmar’s western Rakhine state, where the military has lost control of large areas to the Arakan Army, an ethnic Rakhine armed group.
“Most of the land the Rohingya fled is now held by the Arakan Army, an ethnic Rakhine armed group fighting Naypyitaw. For Rohingya still in Myanmar’s Rakhine State, how the Arakan Army treats them will matter more than anything Naypyitaw says,” Horsey said.
A Rohingya refugee gives a thumbs up while another person holds a placard following the announcement of the International Court of Justice verdict, at a refugee camp in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, Nov. 19, 2026.
(Mohammad Ponir Hossain/REUTERS) Nearly 1.2 million Rohingya remain in refugee camps in Bangladesh, where international aid funding cuts have led to reductions in food rations.
“Hopefully this ruling will be a reminder of their plight to donors, who need to step up,” Horsey said.
Vignoli urged the international community to ensure that the ruling translated into tangible improvements for the persecuted minority.
“Myanmar should swiftly comply with the court’s judgment and end its oppression of the Rohingya. Concerned governments should strongly support the Rohingya and promote justice for atrocities, press Myanmar’s junta to comply with the judgment, and ensure the safe and voluntary return of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.
Update adds Miliband’s statement.

articles.title: HK joins int'l drug standards body
articles.excerpt: The Health Bureau today announced that Hong Kong, China has formally joined the International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements…
articles.fullText:
The Health Bureau today announced that Hong Kong, China has formally joined the International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH) as a regulatory member. The bureau noted that this accession signifies international recognition of the city’s drug research and development (R&D) and regulatory standards.

Joining the ICH will strengthen Hong Kong’s capabilities for the primary evaluation of innovative drugs and allow it to help shape global R&D and registration rules. This milestone will also accelerate the city’s growth into an international health and medical innovation hub.

As an authoritative global body, the ICH harmonises technical requirements for drug registration. It issues safety, efficacy and quality guidelines recognised as the highest international standards for protecting public health.

The ICH approved Hong Kong’s admission as its 20th regulatory member at an assembly meeting in the Czech Republic on November 17, with the city represented by the Pharmacy & Poisons Board of Hong Kong. Other regulatory members include the National Medical Products Administration of China alongside authorities from Europe, Switzerland, the UK and the US.

Secretary for Health Prof Lo Chung-mau said the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government thanked the country for supporting the city’s development into an international health and medical innovation hub. He added that Hong Kong, China becoming a regulatory member demonstrates the unique advantages of the “one country, two systems” principle.

“Since becoming an ICH observer on October 31, 2023, Hong Kong has, with the country’s strong support, devoted its full efforts to fulfilling all the requirements of the ICH, and was able to formally become an ICH regulatory member in just three years, significantly accelerating the process compared with the eight to 10 years estimated by the Government earlier with reference to international experience,” Prof Lo said.

Looking ahead, the health chief noted that the Hong Kong SAR Government will establish the Centre for Medical Products Regulation next month to build independent drug evaluation and approval capacity. The centre will also drive international co-operation to further establish Hong Kong as an international health and medical innovation hub.

articles.title: P1 school results drop next Mon
articles.excerpt: Primary One discretionary places for September 2027 will be released next Monday, the Education Bureau announced today. Of the 32,104…
articles.fullText:
Primary One discretionary places for September 2027 will be released next Monday, the Education Bureau announced today.

Of the 32,104 children who applied for discretionary places at government and aided primary schools, 18,148 will be offered a place.

Among them, 8,270 have siblings studying or parents working at the schools they have applied to. The remaining 9,878 have been selected according to the Points System.

Parents who have already activated their Primary One Admission e-Platform (ePOA) account can check the results via the e-platform from 10am on Monday.

They can also bring a copy of the paper application form and check the results at the school they applied to between 9am and 5pm.

Parents whose children have been offered a discretionary place should register them next Wednesday or Thursday.

For parents whose children have failed to secure a discretionary place or who have opted for Central Allocation only, the bureau will inform them in writing in mid-January 2027 to select schools for Central Allocation via ePOA from January 18 to 24, or at a designated Central Allocation Centre on January 23 or 24.

articles.title: Inflation at 2.2% in October
articles.excerpt: Overall consumer prices rose 2.2% year on year in October, up from the 1.9% increase recorded in September, the Census…
articles.fullText:
Overall consumer prices rose 2.2% year on year in October, up from the 1.9% increase recorded in September, the Census & Statistics Department announced today.

Netting out the effects of the Government’s one-off relief measures, the underlying inflation rate was 2% in October, slightly lower than that in the previous month.

Compared to October 2025, price increases were recorded for electricity, gas and water; miscellaneous services; transport; durable goods; miscellaneous goods; housing; meals out and takeaway food; and clothing and footwear.

Meanwhile, year-on-year decreases were recorded for alcoholic drinks and tobacco, and basic food.

The Government said consumer price inflation stayed moderate in October. While prices of fuel-related items continued to rise noticeably, spillover effects remained limited, with prices of most other items increasing modestly or declining.

Looking ahead, it said earlier increases in international oil prices would continue to feed through to local consumer prices of fuel-related items. However, price pressures on other fronts should remain broadly in check, keeping overall inflation moderate. Nevertheless, geopolitical tensions remain a key source of near-term uncertainty for international fuel prices and warrant close monitoring.

articles.title: Public housing wait falls to 4.4 years
articles.excerpt: The Housing Bureau announced today that the latest Composite Waiting Time for Subsidised Rental Housing (CWT) is 4.4 years, a…
articles.fullText:
The Housing Bureau announced today that the latest Composite Waiting Time for Subsidised Rental Housing (CWT) is 4.4 years, a significant decrease of 0.4 years compared with 4.8 years at the end of June, hitting a new decade low.

This figure is calculated based on the average waiting time of general applicants – family and elderly one-person applicants – who were housed in public rental housing (PRH) or Light Public Housing (LPH) in the past 12 months up to the end of September 2026.

Compared with the peak of 6.1 years before the current-term Government took office, the latest CWT marks a reduction of 1.7 years, falling below 4.5 years for the first time.

In the third quarter of 2026, the bureau arranged for about 11,200 general applicants to be housed in PRH or LPH. These units include 3,100 newly completed PRH flats, about 2,700 recovered PRH flats, and about 5,450 LPH units. Among them, the number of applicants housed in LPH was more than four times that of the previous quarter.

Over the past 12 months, the Government’s overall supply of PRH and LPH has significantly risen to about 8,200 units per quarter, double the average quarterly supply of about 4,100 units during the four years before the current-term Government took office.

During the same period, the waiting time for general applicants housed in PRH was 5.3 years, whereas the waiting time for those housed in LPH was only 2.8 years. The bureau said this clearly demonstrates that the LPH policy has played a key role in faster fulfilment of grassroots citizens’ housing needs.

The bureau highlighted that it is adopting a multipronged approach to expedite the turnover of PRH flats to sustain a downward trend in the number of PRH general applicants.

At the end of September 2026, there were about 96,100 general applications for PRH, representing a significant decrease of nearly 40% compared with the peak of 156,400 cases as of September 2020 – a new 15-year low and the first time the figure has fallen below 100,000 since 2012.

Meanwhile, there were about 80,600 non-elderly one-person applications under the Quota and Points System, representing an even sharper decrease of over 40% compared with the peak of 143,700 cases as of December 2015. The drop among non-elderly one-person applicants aged below 30 was even more pronounced, falling by about 60% over the past decade, from about 70,400 at the end of September 2016 to about 29,300 at the end of September 2026.

The bureau expects to provide an average of over 35,000 units per year in the next five years from 2027-28, representing an increase of about 73% compared with the five-year production since the current-term Government took office, which is the highest in the past 25 years.

Regarding LPH, as of mid-November 2026, about 29,800 units have been completed. The remaining two new projects converted from school premises at Shun Lee Tsuen Road in Kwun Tong and Chuk Yuen Road in Wong Tai Sin – providing a total of about 210 units – are set to be completed in the first quarter of next year. About 30,000 LPH units will be completed in slightly over four years, ahead of the five-year target set out in the 2022 Policy Address.

The bureau noted that, with the continuous increase in overall public housing production and the progressive completion of various PRH and LPH projects, the long-standing backlog of applications is gradually being cleared, resulting in a downward trend in the CWT. It is confident that the target of reducing the CWT to 4.5 years in 2026-27, as announced by the Chief Executive in the 2022 Policy Address, can be achieved.

articles.title: NM ordinance published in Gazette
articles.excerpt: The Northern Metropolis (NM) Development Ordinance was published in the Gazette today, providing the legal basis for facilitation measures that…
articles.fullText:
The Northern Metropolis (NM) Development Ordinance was published in the Gazette today, providing the legal basis for facilitation measures that cover town planning, land compensation, building works approvals, noise control, and cross-boundary flows.

The NM will be developed to serve as a hub for higher education, innovation and technology, while offering an environment suitable for living, working and travelling.

It will act as the main platform for Hong Kong to deeply engage in the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and to actively integrate into and serve overall national development, while serving as a strategic engine to foster economic transformation and develop new quality productive forces.

Passed by the Legislative Council at its third reading on November 12, the ordinance carries great significance for Hong Kong in proactively aligning with the National 15th Five-Year Plan and implementing Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan.

The ordinance aims to expedite development and construction, while helping enterprises establish a presence in the NM.

The Development Bureau and relevant bureaus are formulating the first batch of subsidiary legislation needed to implement these facilitation measures, with a view to tabling it for LegCo's vetting in January and bringing it into effect in the first quarter of 2027.

Pursuant to the provisions of the ordinance that have come into operation, the Secretary for Development has published the plan delineating the NM area on the website . A copy has also been made available at the office of the Land Registry for public inspection.

articles.title: AI risk working group convenes
articles.excerpt: Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki today convened the first meeting of the Working Group on Coordination of AI Risk Governance to…
articles.fullText:
Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki today convened the first meeting of the Working Group on Coordination of AI Risk Governance to comprehensively advance implementation of the policy strategy.

Noting that while artificial intelligence (AI) is developing rapidly, promoting industry upgrades, and improving everyday convenience, Mr Chan stressed that managing its impact across society and prioritising risk governance and application safety are equally crucial.

He said the working group will steer and co-ordinate the efforts of bureaux and departments to examine issues relating to AI development risks, governance, and safety; strengthen public awareness; and develop corresponding management and regulatory frameworks. This aims to ensure that while accelerating technological adoption, these tools are used for good and remain safe and under control.

At the meeting, the working group reviewed and co-ordinated the work plans and implementation proposals for the seven specific actions under the AI risk governance strategy. These cover combating the use of AI in criminal activities, enhancing the protection of minor users, promoting market assessment of ethical issues, ensuring the safe and orderly application of the technology across industries, examining legal liability arising from accidents caused by automated products, introducing guidelines on agent management, and evaluating the impact of automation on employment.

To ensure that Hong Kong's AI risk governance strategy is implemented comprehensively, soundly, and in an orderly manner, the working group will convene regularly as work advances to review and oversee departmental execution of the various measures, and facilitate interdepartmental collaboration.

articles.title: InfraEX Week 2026 opens
articles.excerpt: InfraEX Week 2026, spearheaded by the Development Bureau, opened today. The event aims to establish a premier international exchange platform…
articles.fullText:
InfraEX Week 2026, spearheaded by the Development Bureau, opened today.

The event aims to establish a premier international exchange platform to promote sustainable development, enhance infrastructure delivery efficiency and accelerate the adoption of innovative technologies. It serves as a key catalyst to modernise and transform the construction industry.

Speaking at the grand opening ceremony, Chief Executive John Lee said that in a world shaped by shifting geopolitics, urgent climate challenges and rapid technological advance, ideas must be turned into lasting projects through innovation, collaboration and clear strategic direction.

He added that Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan provides a vital roadmap for the future, giving businesses, investors and innovators clear insight into the city's development and emerging opportunities. He cited the Northern Metropolis, which is central to the Plan, as a prime example of these opportunities.

To build the Northern Metropolis and all that it promises, Mr Lee said Hong Kong must deliver future-ready infrastructure supported by smart city concepts, artificial intelligence, advanced engineering technologies and innovative construction methods and materials. He stressed that collaboration is the most crucial factor for achieving excellence in the construction industry.

Mr Lee then witnessed the exchange of a letter of intent and memoranda of understanding between the Development Bureau and various local and overseas institutions. These agreements will foster deeper cross-regional and cross-sectoral collaboration, laying a solid foundation for more local and Mainland construction enterprises and products to go global.

Vice Minister of the Ministry of Water Resources Liu Dongshun noted at the ceremony that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government announced its First Five-Year Plan in September this year, outlining goals to advance the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), strengthen physical infrastructure connectivity and boost digitalisation and infrastructure resilience. He added that Hong Kong is leveraging its unique advantage of strong national support alongside close global connections to reinforce its position as an international infrastructure hub.

He stressed that the Ministry of Water Resources will deepen exchanges and co-operation with Hong Kong on water-related affairs, providing reliable water security to support the GBA’s high-quality development and safeguard the city’s long-term prosperity and stability.

The Week features three major construction events: its flagship opening event, the 2nd International Infrastructure & Projects Leaders Summit, alongside the International Conference on Modular Construction 2026 and the Construction Innovation Expo 2026.

Held concurrently today, the 2nd International Infrastructure & Projects Leaders Summit is themed “Envisioning a Sustainable Future: From Insights to Impacts”. It explored strategies to tackle industry challenges while driving the sector’s modernisation and high-quality growth.

In her welcome remarks at the Summit luncheon, Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said that under “one country, two systems”, Hong Kong proactively integrates into and serves national development. She added that the city remains committed to its role as a “super-connector” and “super value-adder” to help internationalise national standards and showcase the nation’s innovation and technology to the world.

She noted that the Government is steering the construction industry towards advanced, intelligent and high-quality growth. While accelerating the Northern Metropolis development, the Government is overhauling practices across the board, harnessing artificial intelligence and promoting the widespread adoption of advanced construction materials and technologies.

Permanent Secretary for Development (Works) Ricky Lau said in his keynote presentation at the Summit that the Government is accelerating the Northern Metropolis and other major infrastructure projects, creating vast opportunities for the construction industry.

He noted that as the industry navigates rapid technological shifts, infrastructure upgrades and climate resilience, it is transitioning from traditional delivery models towards a more industrialised, digitalised and tech-enabled phase. This transformation will be driven by three core pillars – innovation, talent development and collaboration – enabling the industry to move forward.

Over 800 major infrastructure project leaders and experts from more than 30 countries and regions attended the Summit, including senior Mainland and overseas government officials as well as representatives from renowned organisations such as the International Institute for Management Development. They shared the latest infrastructure initiatives and challenges at the presentation session and four plenary sessions.

articles.title: Govt firmly rejects US report
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today strongly condemned the 2026 report issued by the United States-China Economic &…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today strongly condemned the 2026 report issued by the United States-China Economic & Security Review Commission (USCC) for its untrue and biased slanders and smears against various aspects of the city’s situation. The Hong Kong SAR Government stressed that it must resolutely refute these claims.

In a statement , the Hong Kong SAR Government stressed that the Hong Kong SAR is an inalienable part of the People's Republic of China. It is a local administrative region that enjoys a high degree of autonomy under "one country, two systems", and comes directly under the Central People's Government.

The statement pointed out that the legal basis for implementing "one country, two systems" comprises the Constitution and the Basic Law, which provide constitutional guarantees for fundamental rights and freedoms, including equality before the law, buttressed by the rule of law and independent judicial power. The Hong Kong SAR Government strongly disapproved of and firmly rejected the USCC's political interference in the affairs of the Hong Kong SAR and its attempts to place politics above law-based administration.

The statement also noted that the Hong Kong SAR steadfastly safeguards national sovereignty, security and development interests, faithfully upholding this top priority of the "one country, two systems" principle. The Hong Kong SAR Government will continue to resolutely, fully and faithfully implement the Hong Kong National Security Law (HKNSL), the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance (SNSO) and other relevant national security laws.

The Hong Kong SAR Government strongly urged the US to discern facts from fallacies, respect international law and basic norms governing international relations, and immediately stop interfering in Hong Kong matters, which are purely China's internal affairs.

The Hong Kong SAR Government also affirmed that it steadfastly safeguards the rights and freedoms enjoyed by Hong Kong residents under the law, which have remained robustly guaranteed by both the Constitution and the Basic Law since Hong Kong’s return to the motherland. The HKNSL and the SNSO serve as institutional foundations for restoring order while safeguarding freedom and development, and law-abiding citizens will not unwittingly violate the law.

The statement noted that the report quoted figures selectively to distort the facts, disregarding the Hong Kong SAR’s persistent commitment to safeguarding the lawful exercise of citizens’ rights and freedoms. The Hong Kong SAR Government stressed it must set the record straight and strongly condemn such actions.

It also pointed out that, since the implementation of the HKNSL and the SNSO, the media landscape in Hong Kong has remained vibrant. Conversely, while the media environment in the US continues to deteriorate, the US and individuals with ulterior motives deliberately fabricated claims regarding press and speech freedoms in Hong Kong.

Regarding the fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, the Hong Kong SAR Government has been pursuing aftermath and relief operations with full force. However, following the blaze, external and anti-China destabilising forces spread false information online and distributed seditious pamphlets in an attempt to smear rescue efforts, sow social division and undermine community unity.

The Hong Kong SAR Government stated that it will not tolerate any malicious smearing or incitement of hatred, and will take decisive enforcement action in accordance with the law.

On national security legislation, the Hong Kong SAR Government stressed that endangering national security is a very serious offence and no country will stand idly by when faced with acts that threaten its security. Indeed, the US itself maintains an extensive and strict national security legal framework.

The statement noted that the USCC applies an entirely different standard to Hong Kong’s national security laws and law enforcement than it does when addressing human rights issues within its own borders. This exposes its double standards as merely political manipulations that must be strongly condemned.

The Hong Kong SAR has a constitutional duty to safeguard national security and must continue to refine its legal system and enforcement mechanisms to do so. The statement said the USCC not only disregards the constitutional duty and practical needs of the Hong Kong SAR to enact and enhance relevant laws, but also criticises the city’s legal system and enforcement mechanisms.

Recently, Hong Kong has hosted numerous mega events, including major international conferences, while international institutions have steadily established headquarters or offices in the city. Coupled with Hong Kong’s strong performance across major international competitiveness and development rankings in recent years, these achievements underscore its status as an international financial and trade centre and reflect broad international confidence, rendering baseless attacks futile.

The statement also emphasised that Hong Kong is a society underpinned by the rule of law. When adjudicating cases involving offences endangering national security, as in any other cases, judges perform their judicial duties independently and impartially, free from any interference, and every defendant has the right to a fair hearing.

Hong Kong has consistently practised free-market economic policies, and its Five-Year Plan reaffirms the city's commitment to a market economy and its global orientation rather than departing from them. The statement stressed that any allegation suggesting Hong Kong is moving away from a capitalist market economy with the introduction of its Five-Year Plan is categorically false.

The statement also reiterated that Hong Kong will continue to leverage its strengths to enhance its role as an international financial, maritime and trade centre, while better integrating into and serving overall national development.

The Hong Kong SAR Government added that it will continue to proactively explore new avenues for economic growth and enhance the city’s competitiveness. In fact, the US enjoys substantial economic benefits in Hong Kong, having recorded a trade surplus of more than US$250 billion with the city over the past 10 years – one of the largest among its global trading partners – with roughly 1,550 US companies currently operating in Hong Kong.

All these figures demonstrate the close, long-standing economic ties between Hong Kong and the US, as well as the vast American business interests in the city. A stable and prosperous Hong Kong is of benefit to Hong Kong and the US, the statement added.

articles.title: Apple Photos AI watermark can tag your real pictures
articles.excerpt: Apple Photos now embeds an invisible SynthID watermark in images edited with Apple Intelligence tools like Clean Up, Extend and…
articles.fullText:
You take a great family photo, but there's one problem. Someone you don't know walked into the background. So you open Apple Photos , use Clean Up to remove the person and save your picture. Problem solved, right? Well, there's something new happening behind the scenes.
With iOS 27.2, Apple Photos can now add an invisible AI watermark to pictures you edit using certain Apple Intelligence tools . You won't see it on your screen. And if you share the photo, the person receiving it probably won't notice anything different either. But the watermark could still be there.
Apple introduced the feature in its Oct. 26 update. It uses Google's SynthID technology to identify images created or modified with artificial intelligence. Even a photo you took yourself can receive this hidden marker after certain AI edits. So how does it work, and what does it mean for the photos you share?
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
STOP LOSING PHOTO QUALITY WHEN YOU SHARE PICTURES
AI photo editing has come a long way. What once required complicated software can now take a few taps on your phone. That's convenient when you want to improve a picture. However, it also makes it harder to tell what's real. Someone can remove an important detail from a photo without leaving an obvious trace. AI can even generate parts of a scene that the camera never captured.
Apple's new watermarking feature gives people a way to tell when AI has been used to create or change an image. According to Apple's official support documentation, certain Apple Intelligence tools now add a hidden SynthID watermark when you create or edit images.
SynthID is technology developed by Google . It embeds a digital signal into an image that compatible detection tools can recognize. The watermark doesn't visibly change your photo. There's no stamp across the bottom or warning in the corner. Instead, the marker remains hidden unless someone checks the image with a SynthID detector.
Apple says the feature applies to certain Apple Intelligence tools starting with iOS 27.2. Here's where you might encounter it.
Clean Up lets you erase distractions from your pictures. Maybe someone wandered into your vacation photo. Or perhaps there's an object in the background you wish you could remove. You can use Clean Up to erase that distraction while AI fills in the missing area. With iOS 27.2, some photos edited this way can receive a SynthID watermark. However, Apple doesn't say that every small edit will trigger one. The watermark can depend on the changes made to the image.
Have you ever taken a picture and realized you were standing too close? Apple's Extend tool can help by generating additional scenery beyond the original edges of your photo. For example, you might have cropped out part of a building. Extend can generate additional background to make the composition look better. The result may look like you captured a wider shot in the first place. However, because AI creates part of the finished image, the photo can receive a hidden SynthID watermark. We've previously explained how Extend works in our article on fixing badly framed photos after you take them.
Apple also includes Spatial Reframing, called Reframe in Photos, among the tools covered by SynthID. Reframe lets you change the apparent perspective of a picture after you've taken it. You can adjust the angle or shift the composition while Apple Intelligence generates the necessary visual information. That can make a photo look quite different from what your camera originally captured. And because AI helps create that result, the edited image may carry a watermark.
Apple's watermarking feature also covers images generated using Image Playground and Image Wand . Image Playground lets you create images with AI using descriptions or other visual inputs. Image Wand can turn a rough sketch into a more developed image. Since these tools generate visual content, their inclusion makes sense. But Apple's decision to mark certain edits to genuine photos raises a more interesting question. Should a real photo receive an AI marker because you removed one distracting object?
NEW YORK MAKES HISTORY WITH FIRST-OF-ITS-KIND LAW REGULATING AI-POWERED COMMERCIALS
You might be wondering whether there's an easy way to see if a photo contains one of these hidden markers. There is, although you'll need to use an online detector. Apple recommends Google's SynthID Detector, which can analyze an uploaded image for the watermark.
One thing to understand: finding a watermark doesn't automatically mean a photo is fake. It simply indicates that AI was involved in creating or modifying the image. And the reverse is also true. If no watermark appears, that doesn't prove the picture is genuine. Other AI image generators may not use SynthID. Detection can also have limitations. I would also be careful about uploading private family pictures or sensitive images to any online service. Review how the service handles uploaded files before submitting them.
Apple says photos created or edited before the 27.2 update won't automatically receive a new SynthID watermark from Apple. So you don't have to worry about the update going through your entire photo library and adding markers to everything.
However, that changes if you open an older picture and edit it using one of the supported AI tools. For example, you could take a photo from five years ago and use Extend to improve the framing today. The newly edited version may then receive the invisible watermark.
Apple has also expanded this feature beyond iPhones. According to the company, SynthID support begins with these software versions: iOS 27.2, iPadOS 27.2, macOS 27.2 and visionOS 27.2. Keep in mind that the software update and Apple Intelligence have different device requirements.
OPENAI CHILD SAFETY TOOLS TARGET AI-GENERATED ABUSE
You'll need an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone to use the editing features that trigger these watermarks. Apple Intelligence works on the iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max, along with iPhone 16 models and newer compatible iPhones. The standard iPhone 15 can install iOS 27.2, but it doesn't support these Apple Intelligence editing features. Availability may also depend on your region and language.
To check for the latest software update:
I like the idea of giving people another way to question what they're seeing online. But there's an important limitation. Let's say you use Clean Up to remove someone standing behind your family in a vacation photo. Now compare that with an AI-generated picture showing an event that never happened. Both images could carry SynthID watermarks, even though the circumstances are very different.
The detector may identify AI involvement. However, it won't necessarily explain what was changed or how significant those changes were. That's a pretty big limitation when you're trying to decide whether to trust an image.
There's also the issue of AI-generated pictures that have no detectable watermark. So, while SynthID can provide a useful clue, it shouldn't be your only way of evaluating a suspicious photo. If a picture online seems questionable, look for the original source. You can also use a reverse image search to see where a photo originally appeared and whether earlier versions exist.
I can see why Apple is doing this. AI has gotten so good at changing photos that it's becoming harder to know what you're actually looking at. And I think that's a real concern. At the same time, I like having tools that can fix a great picture when someone walks into the background. Why should that photo get the same kind of watermark as a picture created entirely by AI? That's where I think Apple could do better. I'd love to see a way to check a photo and find out exactly what AI changed. Was it something minor, or did someone completely alter what happened? That's what I'd want to know before deciding whether to trust what I'm seeing.
Should Apple put a hidden AI watermark on your personal photos simply because you removed something from the background? Or should these markers be reserved for images that AI creates entirely? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

articles.title: Trump, Xi, Putin meeting was a spectacle that yielded little progress: analysts
articles.excerpt: Leaders discussed nuclear tensions, U.S.-China rivalry over AI and Taiwan’s status, but status quo remains.
articles.fullText:
Updated on Nov. 20, 2026 at 12:48 a.m. ET
The leaders of the United States, China and Russia concluded their first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen on Thursday, but their meeting was more about “optics over substance,” experts told Radio Free Asia.
U.S. President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for more than an hour on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, describing the gathering as a historic diplomatic occasion.
Nuclear arms control and regional conflicts were high on the agenda amid deepening geopolitical and technological competition among the world’s major powers.
“As the world’s three largest nuclear powers by far, the United States, Russia and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth and also to lessen the risk that those weapons will ever be used,” Trump said in his opening remarks.
Although the meeting may have been historic, the three leaders have national interests that do not quite align on the nuclear question, David Fedor, a Stephenson Policy Fellow at Stanford University’s Hoover Institution, told RFA.
“Other than President Trump’s comments before the meetings about nuclear weapons, ... there was little signaling ahead of time that substantive decisions would be made,” said Fedor.
Xi called for the prohibition and destruction of nuclear weapons and the establishment of a world free of them, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.
The summit marked the first leader-level talks on nuclear arms control since New START expired in February. Its lapse ended the last remaining bilateral nuclear treaty between Washington and Moscow, raising concerns about an unrestricted arms race.
Trump Xi Putin trilateral in China
Trump has called for a new agreement that would bring Beijing into nuclear arms control negotiations. China, however, has long maintained that Washington and Moscow should substantially reduce their stockpiles before asking it to accept limitations on its comparatively smaller arsenal.
China is estimated to possess more than 600 nuclear warheads, while the United States and Russia hold more than 5,000 each.
“Once you have the nuclear weapons, it’s very hard not to have them,” Trump said. “So it’s not an easy thing to do, give them up.”
Xi also proposed regular high-level exchanges and the creation of a crisis communication mechanism among the three powers to help manage tensions.
No concrete agreement on nuclear arms control was immediately announced following the summit.
The White House released a statement that said the three leaders “reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.”
Russian President Vladimir Putin attends a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Leaders' Summit in Shenzhen, China, November 19, 2026.
(Vyacheslav Prokofyev/Sputnik via Reuters) The statement also said that the three countries would hold dialogues on preventing the spread of nuclear weapons and minimizing nuclear risks.
Taiwan’s security concerns
Ahead of Thursday’s trilateral meeting, Taiwan’s government downplayed expectations that the island would feature prominently in discussions among the three leaders.
“From what we know, Taiwan is not the focus,” Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) spokesperson Liang Wen-chieh told a news briefing in Taipei.
Liang said the discussions were more likely to prioritize securing a ceasefire in Ukraine and addressing Iran’s nuclear program.
“Even if Taiwan is mentioned, it will be a relatively peripheral issue,” he said.
Liang also expressed doubts about whether the three leaders could reach substantive agreements given their competing interests and the limited time available for negotiations.
“The three parties want different things, and their priorities are also different,” he said.
Taiwan nevertheless featured in a separate bilateral meeting between Trump and Xi earlier on Thursday, their third face-to-face meeting this year.
Xi told Trump that Washington should “stick to doing the right thing” on Taiwan to avoid major setbacks in relations between the two countries, China’s official Xinhua News Agency reported.
According to Xinhua, Trump told Xi that the United States “does not support Taiwan independence.”
The White House had not released its own account of the bilateral meeting at the time of Xinhua’s report.
These statements, and others on Ukraine, seemed to be a repeat of previous statements, Ian Chong, an associate professor of political science at the National University of Singapore, told RFA.
" This whole series of meetings have been big on optics and small on deliverables," said Chong. “⁠⁠There were general declaratory statements but little visible substantive progress, at least on to the public. ... I suppose repeating the basic principles are better than nothing."
People pass a sign for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, Nov. 17, 2026.
(Pedro Pardo/AFP) During the trilateral summit, Xi also called on major powers to respect each other’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and core interests, warning against crossing red lines on sensitive issues.
Taiwan, which joined APEC in 1991 under the name Chinese Taipei, is represented at this year’s summit by Acer founder and honorary chairman Stan Shih, appointed by President Lai Ching-te to attend on his behalf.
The lack of substance in statements regarding Taiwan was likely an outcome Taipei was hoping for, William Yang, senior analyst for North East Asia at the Belgium-based International Crisis Group.
“On Taiwan, an issue where there is very little basis for bilateral consensus, they basically treated it as a formality — something they had to mention briefly as part of the routine agenda, and then move on,” said Yang. “I think, overall, when the two sides’ readouts came out yesterday, the immediate reaction from the Taiwan government was probably one of relief.”
Neither Xi’s nor Trump’s statement did much to change the status quo for Taiwan, he said.
“Basically, Taiwan made it through another Trump-Xi meeting without any rhetoric being put forward that would cause major harm to Taiwan.”
Competition over artificial intelligence
The summit took place against a backdrop of mounting technological rivalry between Washington and Beijing, particularly over artificial intelligence (AI) and access to advanced semiconductors.
Trump has held off on imposing tougher restrictions on China’s access to advanced chips used to develop AI models, indicating that additional measures could aggravate bilateral tensions.
Xi urged Washington and Moscow to work with Beijing to maintain stable global supply chains and called on the three powers to “abandon Cold War mentality, not pursue decoupling and breaking chains.”
Competition over emerging technologies has become a major point of friction between the world’s two largest economies, alongside disagreements over trade and access to strategically important raw materials.
China's President Xi Jinping, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russia's President Vladimir Putin arrive for a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, Nov. 19, 2026.
(Doug Mills/AFP) U.S. officials have accused Beijing of failing to fully implement commitments made during a Trump-Xi meeting last year, including pledges to purchase more American agricultural products and ease export restrictions on rare earth minerals used in electronics manufacturing.
A trade truce reached last year following successive tariff increases is due to expire on Jan. 10, 2027, adding another source of uncertainty to bilateral relations.
The meeting between Xi and Trump did little to ease this uncertainty, Riley Walters, deputy director of the Japan Chair at the Washington-based Hudson Institute, told RFA.
“It sounds like Trump and U.S. officials are still waiting on China to buy more soybeans and export more rocks, meaning maybe no progress is being made since their last meeting,” said Riley.
“Instead, it sounds like Trump and Xi simply meeting and talking has become the baseline for this relationship, and so long as they continue meeting then it’s construction.”
Fedor said that Trump seems to feel a sense of responsibility in managing relationships with Xi and Putin.
That sentiment is what drives him to ”stage these very public interactions with leaders like Chairman Xi and President Putin," he said.
“But I do not think those visits substantively change the underlying interests of the relevant parties, at least some of which are fundamentally contradictory.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.
Update adds comments from experts.

articles.title: Trilateral summit positive, constructive, fruitful: Xi
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping on Thursday said that the China-Russia-US summit has been positive, constructive and fruitful. The president made the…
articles.fullText:
President Xi Jinping on Thursday said that the China-Russia-US summit has been positive, constructive and fruitful.

The president made the remarks while summarising main consensus reached at the summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen.

Xi said the three countries shared the same view on safeguarding world peace, and stressed that the hard-won peace must be cherished.

They all agreed that major countries should take the legitimate security concerns of every country seriously, and that dialogue and negotiation are the right choice to resolve differences, the president added.

"There is hope for peace as long as dialogue does not cease and the door does not close," Xi said.

The president urged the three countries to follow through on the consensus reached at the summit, continue to strengthen communication, promote peace through cooperation, and work together to build a better world.

Meanwhile, Putin said that Russia stands ready to work with China and the US to contribute to world peace and security, promote free and open international trade, safeguard energy and food security, and strengthen international cooperation on artificial intelligence governance.

He said the victory in World War Two brought the three countries together, while safeguarding the purposes and principles of the United Nations Charter and upholding international peace are their shared responsibilities.

In a statement, the White House said the three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security.

Washington added that the three countries planned to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the "benefit of all nations".

"The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought," the statement said, and that the three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. (Xinhua and agencies)

Edited by Raymond Yeung

The leaders of China, the United States and Russia held trilateral talks on the sidelines of the final day of the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting.

RTHK reporter Hailey Yip and CGTN's Yang Chengxi sum up the highlights for Thursday, November 19.

articles.title: HK, Singapore leaders meet on Apec sidelines
articles.excerpt: The leaders of Hong Kong and Singapore on Thursday discussed fostering closer ties on the sidelines of the Apec summit…
articles.fullText:
The leaders of Hong Kong and Singapore on Thursday discussed fostering closer ties on the sidelines of the Apec summit.

Chief Executive John Lee said in his meeting with Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong that they discussed Hong Kong’s first five-year plan.

“I’m thankful because it just strengthened our partnership and relationship,” Lee said.

Wong, for his part, said exchanges between the two governments have continued at various levels, such as the Singapore-Hong Kong Permanent Secretaries Exchange Programme which was held in Singapore in July.

“The ties are warmer than ever, and I look forward to building even closer cooperation between our two cities,” he said.

Lee agreed that the exchange programme was working very well and suggested that next year’s exchange take place in Hong Kong.

In his social media post, Lee thanked Singapore for its continued support for the SAR’s early accession to Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), as the Lion City takes up the Asean chairmanship next year.

“I welcome Singapore’s public and private sectors, including GIC and technology enterprises, to explore the business potential of the Hong Kong Park in the Hetao Co-operation Zone and deepen collaboration in areas such as artificial intelligence and biotechnology,” he wrote.

The CE said the two cities are both outward-oriented economies with strong track records in finance, trade and shipping.

He said commercial ties between the two cities are close, and that he looked forward to the further consolidation of their partnership.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Takaichi wants 'constructive, stable' ties with China
articles.excerpt: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, on her first trip to China since taking office, said on Thursday that she intends…
articles.fullText:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, on her first trip to China since taking office, said on Thursday that she intends to build a "constructive and stable relationship" with Beijing.

Her trip to Shenzhen for the Apec summit was also her first to China since making comments about Taiwan a year ago that caused a sharp deterioration in relations with Beijing.

"We intend to comprehensively advance our strategic and mutually beneficial relationship... pursuing dialogue to safeguard the national interests of both sides, and build a constructive and stable relationship," Takaichi said on the sidelines of the summit.

"China is an important neighbour," she said, adding that "precisely because there are pending issues and challenges between Japan and China, we believe it is important to engage in dialogue and maintain communication." (AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: HK, mainland stocks fall amid chip clampdown
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong's benchmark sank to four-month lows while mainland stocks remained under pressure, as fresh trade tensions flared up between…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong's benchmark sank to four-month lows while mainland stocks remained under pressure, as fresh trade tensions flared up between China and the United States despite meetings between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump in Shenzhen.

The benchmark Hang Seng Index closed 453 points, or 1.9 percent, down at 22,841 on turnover of HK$229.55 billion.

The tech index fell 87 points, or 2.3 percent, to 3,649, hitting a 26-month low as it extended its losing streak to seven sessions, while the China enterprises index stumbled 145 points, or 1.9 percent, to 7,690.

Hong Kong-listed AI model developers and AI hyperscalers, whose competitiveness depends on advanced computing power, tumbled.

MiniMax slumped as much as 11 percent to record lows while Z.AI lost two percent.

Tencent tumbled nearly seven percent to a 31-month low after its third-quarter revenue missed forecasts, and the company said new US chip curbs may slow model training.

Alibaba tanked 5.5 percent to a 22-month low while Shanghai Iluvatar CoreX Semiconductor slumped 17 percent.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index fell 10 points, or 0.28 percent, to close at 3,577, its lowest level, in more than 15 months on turnover of 636.9 billion yuan.

The Shenzhen Component Index dropped 76 points, or 0.71 percent, to close at 10,583 on turnover of 668.23 billion yuan while the ChiNext Index declined 18 points, or 0.79 percent, to close at 2,293 on turnover of 310.12 billion yuan.

Tech stocks that rely on advanced chips, including cloud computing, AI and big data, led the declines

The losses came as Xi said on Thursday he remained committed to working with Trump to steer ties between their countries on the "correct course", even as the Commerce Ministry voiced strong opposition to a recent series of economic and trade restrictions the US imposed against China.

The Nvidia saga has led to tighter scrutiny of US chip exports to China.

The Trump administration is also considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models to discourage reliance on the technology.

Meanwhile, a US House panel asked Microsoft on Wednesday to brief lawmakers on a report that said the company could allow the Chinese firm ByteDance to use OpenAI models through Microsoft's Azure cloud platform.

These developments deepened investor worry that the world's two largest economies are careening towards a fresh tit-for-tat trade war, after the Republicans' defeat in the US midterms appears to have prompted the White House to take a more hawkish policy towards China.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei ended 419 points, or 0.71 percent, higher at 59,444, with Softbank Group gaining 4.5 percent and Advantest edging down 0.55 percent. The broader Topix edged down 0.04 percent to 3,822 in, like with the Nikkei, similarly choppy trading.

In Seoul, the Kospi recovered from early losses to end 70 points, or 1.39 percent, higher on a rebound by chipmakers, with Samsung Electronics rising 1.13 percent and SK Hynix gaining 3.41 percent. (Agencies)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Xi says China-US ties 'generally stable and positive'
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping on Thursday said that China-US relations have generally maintained a stable and positive trajectory, injecting stability and…
articles.fullText:
President Xi Jinping on Thursday said that China-US relations have generally maintained a stable and positive trajectory, injecting stability and certainty into the world.

The president made the remarks when meeting with his US counterpart Donald Trump on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen.

Xi said that he and Trump had jointly explored the right way for China and the United States, as two major countries, to get along, established a new positioning of a constructive bilateral relationship of strategic stability and given it new meaning based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, according to Xinhua News Agency.

The new positioning has been welcomed by the people of both countries and by the international community, he added.

Trump said the two leaders have jointly guided the development of bilateral relations, and both sides should maintain the positive momentum of the stable development in ties.

Xi also said the US "must keep doing the right thing" on Taiwan to avoid setbacks in ties with Beijing.

"On the Taiwan issue, the United States must keep doing the right thing to avoid the emergence of great turbulence in the China-US relationship," Xinhua quoted Xi as saying.

Trump told Xi that Washington does not support "Taiwan independence".

On artificial intelligence, Xi told his US counterpart that the two countries should cooperate to keep AI "under human control".

"China and the United States should strengthen communication and coordination to guard against artificial intelligence safety risks and ensure that artificial intelligence always remains under human control," Xi said. (Additional reporting by AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Xi, Putin, Trump kick off landmark trilateral talks
articles.excerpt: The leaders of China, Russia and the United States have opened historic three-way talks aimed at safeguarding world peace. The…
articles.fullText:
The leaders of China, Russia and the United States have opened historic three-way talks aimed at safeguarding world peace.

The meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump was held on Thursday afternoon in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the Apec summit.

In his opening remarks, Xi said the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the Chinese, Russian and US heads of state is of groundbreaking significance.

"As major countries in the world and permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, our three countries should set a good example, cooperate in responding to global challenges, jointly safeguard world peace and stability, and make greater contributions to human progress," he said.

Xi also said peace among major countries brings stability to the world, while their contention would only lead to chaos.

He made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace – they should uphold mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation.

Putin said their three nations shared an "interest" in resolving the Ukraine war and a "responsibility" for global peace and security.

Trump said the three leaders were "making history" by holding talks in Shenzhen.

The trilateral meeting came after Trump held separate one-on-one talks with Putin and Xi earlier in the day.

The wars in Iran and Ukraine as well as nuclear disarmament are expected to be on the agenda. (Xinhua and agencies)

articles.title: Five positive outcomes for HK at Apec summit: Lee
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee on Thursday outlined five outcomes for the SAR at this year’s Apec meetings in Shenzhen. They…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee on Thursday outlined five outcomes for the SAR at this year’s Apec meetings in Shenzhen.

They are: contributing Hong Kong's strengths by actively participating in and supporting the country's successful hosting of the Apec meetings; deepening exchanges and cooperation with Apec member economies; consolidating relations with Asean member states; further exploring emerging markets; and telling the good stories of the Greater Bay Area.

"My takeaway is that Hong Kong's development resonates with our country's development. As an international city and international financial centre, we can serve the country's needs with our unique advantages and what Hong Kong does best," Lee said.

"We are pressing ahead with four centres development and one hub development, contributing to our country's high-quality development. Therefore, we shall actively integrate with and serve our national development, and at the same time, we will strengthen our connectivity with the international world."

Lee noted that he met leaders from a number of Apec member economies through bilateral meetings.

On Wednesday, he met with the leaders of Malaysia, Vietnam, Brunei, Thailand and Chile, and is set to hold talks with leaders from Peru and Singapore on Thursday afternoon.

The CE said he has briefed them on opportunities within the Greater Bay Area, with the talks focusing on strengthening bilateral ties and addressing topics of mutual concern.

Lee said during his meeting with the president of Chile, they jointly witnessed the signing of a Working Holiday Scheme agreement between the two sides, the first of its kind between the SAR and Latin America.

Lee added that the opportunity to meet five Asean leaders would boost Hong Kong's bid to join the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership.

The chief executive also noted that he held a brief conversation with President Xi Jinping, updating him on the panel discussion regarding the Greater Bay Area at the Apec CEO Summit.

Lee said he told Xi the session received a very positive response, with participants agreeing on the massive opportunities available across the region.

Lee said he assured the president that Hong Kong will continue to serve as a "super-connector" and "super value-adder" to better serve and integrate into national development.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Xi, Trump hold talks in Shenzhen
articles.excerpt: Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump opened talks in Shenzhen on Thursday afternoon, the third meeting between the leaders of…
articles.fullText:
Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump opened talks in Shenzhen on Thursday afternoon, the third meeting between the leaders of China and the United States this year.

The meeting on the sidelines of the Apec summit came shortly after Trump held one-on-one talks with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin.

And the three leaders are set to hold a landmark trilateral meeting later in the afternoon.

"You are my friend and we have a very special relationship," Trump told Xi ahead of their talks.

"China-US relations have remained generally stable and improved, bringing tangible benefits to the people of both countries and injecting stability and certainty into the world," Xi said.

The meeting lasted roughly an hour, after which the two leaders and their delegations had lunch. (Agencies)
