Hong Kong's stock market ended lower on Wednesday, with the benchmark Hang Seng Index down 0.91 percent to close at 23,294 points.

The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index dropped 0.86 percent, and the Hang Seng Tech Index slid 0.58 percent.

On the mainland, the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index finished up 0.09 percent while the Shenzhen Component Index closed 0.2 percent higher.

In Japan, Tokyo stocks ended mixed, as stronger-than-expected earnings from US chipmaker Nvidia lifted investor sentiment, while lingering uncertainty over the artificial intelligence sector kept risk appetite in check.

The Nikkei ended up 163 points, or 0.28 percent, at 59,024.

The broader Topix index, meanwhile, fell 16 points, or 0.42 percent, to close at 3,824.

Japanese stocks fluctuated throughout the day as investors weighed optimism over Nvidia's latest earnings against persistent concerns about the outlook for AI-related stocks.

Nvidia reported record quarterly net profit and revenue, easing concerns over the profitability and sustainability of massive investments in AI infrastructure.

However, uncertainty surrounding the company's leadership transition following Jensen Huang's departure, along with concerns over potential AI regulations in the United States, continued to weigh on investor sentiment. (Xinhua)

articles.title: 'HK has key role in keeping global shipping stable'
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong will play an important part in keeping world shipping stable and fast-tracking the sector's green transition, said John…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong will play an important part in keeping world shipping stable and fast-tracking the sector's green transition, said John Denholm, chairman of the International Chamber of Shipping (ICS), in a recent interview with Xinhua.

"The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area is a fantastic economic engine. I'm sure that Hong Kong, as a main port in the Greater Bay Area, will grow from strength to strength," Denholm told Xinhua on the sidelines of the World Maritime Merchants Forum 2026.

Hong Kong's commitment to free trade made it a popular place to do business, Denholm said.

It is also a staunch supporter of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea as well as the International Maritime Organisation's regulatory framework, which are essential to making world trade flourish, especially when heightened geopolitical tensions jeopardise freedom of navigation, said Denholm.

Denholm also applauded Hong Kong's pledge to advance the green transition of shipping.

The city aims to see the proportion of its registered vessels using green maritime fuels reach seven percent by 2030.

Denholm expects the use of green fuels to grow fast as the shipping industry is committed to achieving net-zero emissions by around 2050.

Hong Kong is poised to make green maritime fuel more available to the industry with the support of the world-leading shipbuilding capacity and green technologies of the Chinese mainland, according to Denholm.

In the first three quarters of this year, Chinese shipyards secured 81.8 percent of the world's new shipbuilding orders.

China also has the potential to become a major supplier of green fuel, said Denholm.

At the opening ceremony of the World Maritime Merchants Forum 2026 on Monday, Hong Kong inked an agreement with the Port of Piraeus in Greece to jointly establish a Green Shipping Corridor.

Denholm called Hong Kong's partnership with other ports to provide clean fuel a "fantastic start" to promote the green revolution. (Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: South China Sea code of conduct could depend on landlocked Laos: analysts
articles.excerpt: ASEAN meetings again ended without a code of conduct, and Vientiane might have influence in future negotiations.
articles.fullText:
Landlocked Laos could play a huge role in future negotiations between ASEAN and China on a South China Sea code of conduct, potentially tipping the scales for Beijing, but close ties with its northern neighbor do not mean that Vientiane is acting as a proxy to block negotiations, analysts told Radio Free Asia.
As the leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN, concluded their summit in Manila this week, the bloc again failed to finalize the code of conduct, or COC – an agreement that would seek to prevent confrontations in the sea which is claimed in its entirety by China and in part by Vietnam, the Philippines, Brunei and Malaysia.
The COC has been in negotiations for decades, and hammering out the agreement during this week’s meeting was a priority for the bloc’s current chair, the Philippines, a country with an exclusive economic zone, or EEZ, that significantly overlaps the territory claimed by China within its nine-dash line. Philippines foreign minister Ma. Theresa Lazaro on Nov. 15 told reporters that about 80% of a draft of the code had been completed.
But the agreement will have to wait until at least next year, when the next ASEAN meeting will be held in Singapore.
The overlapping claims of China and the Philippines in the South China Sea.
(AFP) Laos as an ASEAN member state wields significant influence despite not having any claims in the South China Sea, as the bloc operates on a consensus system. Vientiane’s deepening economic and military ties with China could make it sympathetic to Beijing’s foreign policy goals, Joseph Kristanto, a research analyst at Singapore’s S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, told RFA.
“For China, having a sympathetic voice within ASEAN could therefore be useful, particularly in shaping the language and provisions of the eventual agreement, rather than necessarily obstructing the negotiations outright,” he said.
Influence does not mean control
Kristanto said Laos could influence ASEAN’s collective position by objecting to clauses supported by claimant countries, but he cautioned against treating that capacity, or its growing relationship with China, as proof that it was exercising influence at Beijing’s direction.
“While its growing economic and military ties with China could give Beijing considerable influence, I’d say that currently there is insufficient evidence to conclude that Vientiane is deliberately obstructing the COC negotiations on Beijing’s behalf,” he said.
Laos also has interests that could limit its alignment with China, particularly its longstanding political and security relationship with Vietnam and its standing within ASEAN, Kristanto added.
Although the bloc’s charter establishes consultation and consensus as its basic decision-making principle, it also allows the ASEAN summit to decide how a specific decision can be made when consensus fails. Additionally, disagreements over sensitive issues can complicate a common position.
An Oct. 12, 2025, photo distributed by the Philippine Coast Guard shows a China coast guard ship, right, deploying a water cannon at a Philippine Bureau of Fisheries vessel near Thitu Island in disputed waters of the South China Sea.
(Philippine Coast Guard via AFP) Still, if in future negotiations China were to push for a less binding code and faced resistance, Laos could oppose ASEAN decisions or joint statements to help reshape the agreement, Enrico Cau, a Taipei-based independent security researcher, told RFA.
“Much like Cambodia, Laos seems to be closely aligned to China,” said Cau.
He explained that Chinese investment and expanding security ties support a relationship that also serves the interests of Lao and Cambodian leaders: alignment with Beijing could help sustain their governments and support development without requiring democratic reforms.
Cau therefore saw little reason to expect either country to make a fundamental shift away from supporting China within ASEAN. His assessment pointed to potential influence over future decisions, rather than identifying a specific Lao intervention in the current negotiations.
A different regional climate
Comparisons with Cambodia draw on the breakdown of an ASEAN foreign ministers’ meeting in Phnom Penh in 2012. The meeting ended without a joint communiqué for the first time in the bloc’s history after disagreements over South China Sea language. Manila accused Cambodia, then the chair, of opposing references to Beijing taking control of Scarborough Shoal, a maritime feature within the Philippines’ EEZ.
Cambodia at that time described it as a “bilateral dispute” rather than a multilateral issue involving the whole of ASEAN.
Phnom Penh continued to veto drafts of the communiqué that included mentions of the shoal, Manila refused to sign off on versions that excluded it, and the meeting concluded in disagreement.
The following year, the Philippines took the issue to an international arbitral tribunal in The Hague, which issued a ruling in 2016 that invalidated Beijing’s claims based on the nine-dash line. China has rejected the ruling and continues to control the shoal.
Although Cambodia blocked an ASEAN communiqué that would have criticized China in 2012, the bloc is less likely to criticize China these days, Chong Ja Ian, a political scientist at the National University of Singapore and non-resident scholar at Carnegie China, told RFA.
“Laos could take a blocking role but the context is somewhat different,” he said. “There is less appetite across ASEAN for criticizing Beijing today.”
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., center, and first lady Louise Araneta-Marcos, right, greet Laos Prime Minister Saleumxay Kommasith and his wife Alouny Kommasith upon arriving for the 49th ASEAN Summit, in Manila, Philippines, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026
(Ezra Acayan/Getty Images via AP) Unpredictability in the U.S. alongside China’s ability and willingness to exert pressure on ASEAN has made the bloc’s governments less willing to openly differ with Beijing, with the Philippines a notable exception, Chong said.
While most of the ASEAN member states have publicly stated their commitments to a substantive code of conduct, Chong questioned whether this was in fact the case. Some might wish to appear cooperative while remaining lukewarm about an agreement whose obligations and enforcement were unclear, he said.
That uncertainty could complicate efforts to distinguish Chinese influence through Laos from wider disagreements within ASEAN itself, according to Chong.
Both Washington and Beijing have in the past made efforts to secure Lao support for their respective Southeast Asia policy goals. During Laos’s ASEAN chairmanship in 2016, then-U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry visited Vientiane and emphasized ASEAN unity and maritime rights. Months later, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi publicly claimed support from Laos, Cambodia and Brunei for resolving maritime disputes through talks among directly concerned countries.
ASEAN Philippines: key takeaways
For future South China Sea negotiations, the analysts said that Laos’s role must also be judged against what an eventual code would achieve.
Chong said a largely declaratory agreement would likely have limited effects on China’s behavior at sea, meaning Laos’s actions might make less difference than the underlying weaknesses of the document. Cau argued that an initial agreement could still provide a foundation for improvements over time.
Kristanto said the central question was whether Laos could influence the substance of the eventual agreement, rather than simply delay its completion.
“After all, concluding a COC and concluding an effective COC are two different things, particularly when contentious issues such as its legal status, geographical scope, and implementation remain unresolved.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Declines in Asia as Nvidia results fail to reassure
articles.excerpt: Local and mainland shares were mixed at the start of trade on Wednesday as equities failed to capitalise on blockbuster…
articles.fullText:
Local and mainland shares were mixed at the start of trade on Wednesday as equities failed to capitalise on blockbuster earnings from Nvidia that soothed concerns about the AI boom, but have been overshadowed by the resignation of its CEO Jensen Huang who admitted to a bunch of extra-marital affairs.

In Hong Kong, Hang Seng Index lost 79 points, or 0.34 percent, to open at 23,428.

Up north, shares began the day higher with the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index up 0.33 percent while the Shenzhen Component Index opened 0.37 percent higher.

In a highly anticipated earnings release on Tuesday, US tech giant Nvidia said third-quarter revenue topped expectations and doubled to more than US$115 billion while net profit hit US$65.3 billion.

The firm also increased its forecast for next year's revenue, predicting 75 percent growth, compared with a previous forecast of 70 percent.

Still, despite the positive results, Japan's Nikkei average reversed early gains to trade lower, as concerns about the outlook for AI development in the US and Nvidia's leadership outweighed the chip maker's robust outlook.

The Nikkei was down 0.72 percent, after earlier rising as much as 1.3 percent.

The broader Topix also turned lower, down 1.02 percent.

Nvidia shares rose nearly five percent in after-hours trading after the chipmaker, seen as a bellwether for the AI sector, reported quarterly revenue above forecasts in its first earnings report since Huang's abrupt departure as CEO this month.

Also, Nvidia's leadership signalled they would brook no dissent in their plan to find a new CEO, rejecting a "Stand With Jensen" campaign from allies of Huang, even as the Wall Street Journal reported a regulator was probing Nvidia.

"The momentum in Japan that was lifted by a strong outlook for Nvidia did not last long. The market was concerned about the fate of Jensen Huang," said Kazuaki Shimada, chief strategist at IwaiCosmo Securities.

"And a possible slowdown of US data centre construction weighed on investor sentiment, while the market also wanted to wait to see how Anthropic's IPO would proceed," he said. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Xi urges efforts to build a prosperous Asia-Pacific
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping on Wednesday said China is willing to work with all parties to forge ahead with greater confidence…
articles.fullText:
President Xi Jinping on Wednesday said China is willing to work with all parties to forge ahead with greater confidence and resolve to jointly build an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together.

Xi made the remarks in a keynote speech at the Apec CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen.

The president called for maintaining peace and stability – and building a bridge of openness and cooperation – for the Asia-Pacific to prosper together.

"Stability brings security; security brings prosperity," Xi said.

"The Asia-Pacific economy has maintained a stable and positive trajectory, becoming a key engine of global economic growth thanks to a long-term stable regional environment. The more complex the external situation becomes, the more resolutely we must uphold the post-war international order."

He said the region should support free and open trade and investment, adding that efforts should be made to eliminate trade and investment barriers to foster an open Asia-Pacific economy.

"History shows that openness brings progress, while isolation inevitably leads to backwardness. We must resolutely uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organisation at its core, support free and open trade and investment, and safeguard the stability and smooth functioning of global industrial and supply chains."

Xi called for efforts to steadily advance the process of the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific.

Xi stressed the need to inject momentum into innovation-driven growth, and that efforts should be made to develop sci-tech innovation partnerships, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence, and promote green and low-carbon transition.

He called on the region to expand pathways to mutual benefits and win-win outcomes to prosper together.

Xi said China supports the establishment of a world association for bay areas economic cooperation, so as to deepen exchanges and interactions among various bay areas and explore new paths of Asia-Pacific economic cooperation.

"The Asia-Pacific region is home to the world's most important bay areas notable for their open and interconnected economies with positive spillover effects."

He also urged resolving differences through dialogue and consultation, and addressing challenges through solidarity and coordination.

The president added that China's 15th Five-Year Plan presents a list of opportunities for economic growth of the Asia-Pacific and beyond, describing the development blueprint as an invitation for cooperation extended to the global business community.

China will provide the global business community with its super-sized, open market, broad development prospects, as well as a cooperative environment that promotes mutual progress, he said.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Pochettino ends USA tenure, heads to Manchester
articles.excerpt: Mauricio Pochettino's reign as United States coach ended with a simple 2-0 win over Haiti on Tuesday, sent off in…
articles.fullText:
Mauricio Pochettino's reign as United States coach ended with a simple 2-0 win over Haiti on Tuesday, sent off in style by a Christian Pulisic bicycle kick as he heads to his new role at Manchester United.

Teenager Julian Hall also added his fifth goal from six games to secure an 8-0 aggregate victory in the Concacaf Nations League quarter-final second leg in Cincinnati, with Pochettino set to fly to England just hours after the final whistle.

Pochettino, who steered the US to the last-16 of a home World Cup this summer, picked a strong lineup for his swansong and his favoured stars appeared determined to wave their coach off with a win, beginning with high intensity.

A bright Weston McKennie missed two good early chances, before turning creator in the 25th minute for Pulisic's opener.

Pulisic stole possession on the halfway line and surged up the left flank before feeding the ball inside.

McKennie crossed back into the box from the right and Pulisic, running away from goal, improvised a bicycle kick over his left shoulder that bounced in off the far post.

Striker Hall doubled the lead in the 43rd minute. McKennie again provided the assist, chipping the ball over the Haitian backline.

Hall did well to trap the ball, chest it down and then lift it over the goalkeeper. The 18-year-old has scored on all four US starts.

After the break Auston Trusty had a header acrobatically cleared off the line by Martin Experience. Video replays seemed to show it crossing over, but no goal was awarded.

Defensive midfielder Sebastian Berhalter picked up a yellow for a sliding challenge that rules him out of the semi-final in March.

Alex Freeman, the 22-year-old defender given his debut by Pochettino who has become a stalwart at right-back, did superbly to intercept a clear-cut chance for Josue Casimir.

Hall's header in the final few minutes bounced off the crossbar.

The often emotional Pochettino, who had issued a message before the game thanking US fans "from the bottom of my heart", calmly applauded Pulisic's spectacular strike, before exchanging warm hugs and smiles with his staff at the final whistle.

More testing challenges lie ahead, with United languishing in 18th place in the Premier League and due to face bitter rivals Liverpool on Sunday.

Pochettino is expected to head directly to United's Carrington training facility on arrival. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Springboks coach Erasmus handed six-game ban
articles.excerpt: South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus was handed a six-game ban by World Rugby on Tuesday for outspoken criticism of officials…
articles.fullText:
South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus was handed a six-game ban by World Rugby on Tuesday for outspoken criticism of officials following a rare defeat for the world champions against France.

Erasmus questioned the decision by the television match official not to intervene on a series of French tackles during his side's 21-19 loss in Paris.

"If he didn't see it, it must be a technology problem. If he saw it and decided not to act on it, is that not match-fixing?" he said in a press conference in Dublin on Monday, ahead of the Springboks' clash against Ireland this weekend.

The 54-year-old will be banned from "any match-day involvement" with his players and coaches and will not be allowed to even enter the stadium.

"The panel determined that the conduct clearly amounts to disrespecting the authority of the match officials by impugning their integrity," World Rugby said in a statement.

"Teams have access to well-established and supported channels and protocols for raising officiating matters before and after matches.

"Challenging a decision is not the same as questioning an official's integrity or making comments that expose them to personal abuse."

Erasmus is no stranger to disciplinary action for taking aim at officials.

In 2021, he was banned from all rugby activity for two months by World Rugby for an hour-long video criticising the refereeing in the Springboks' first Test defeat by the British and Irish Lions.

The following year, he received a two-match ban for a series of social media posts criticising officials in a defeat by France.

South Africa Rugby has requested a full misconduct hearing.

"The organisation respected the process but had requested an opportunity for its coach to contextualise his comments and assure the panel that it was not his intention to allege that any match official had acted with ulterior motives," said a spokesperson for SA Rugby.

Erasmus could miss the final of the Nations Championship on November 29.

South Africa trail New Zealand by one point at the top of the southern hemisphere standings with one round of fixtures to go.

The other four matches are likely to be South Africa's opening fixtures of the 2027 Rugby Championship campaign, freeing Erasmus up to return in time for next year's World Cup in Australia. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Tech outage wave continues, as Trump says all is fine
articles.excerpt: Technology outages that shut down email for many companies and grounded thousands of flights over the past few days extended…
articles.fullText:
Technology outages that shut down email for many companies and grounded thousands of flights over the past few days extended to the US National Security Agency on Tuesday, as US President Donald Trump's administration downplayed concerns about a broader problem.

The NSA said its network experienced a "temporary degradation" during routine maintenance, but that "mission-critical capabilities" remained operational. The series of disruptions to critical systems, which also touched the banking system on Monday, prompted even some Trump allies to demand more information.

"If this is all a coincidence, it's like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world," US Senator Josh Hawley, a Missouri Republican, told reporters.

Trump earlier played down the incidents, which raised questions of whether the government and private sector had moved too quickly in cutting tech staff.

"It's like when you're big and powerful, and you have all the money. Things like that happen. It's fine," Trump told reporters in Manila, where he was attending the Asean economic conference.

Technology-related disruptions have hit every weekday since Thursday, when a Microsoft outage disrupted many of its services, including email.

The next day, the Federal Aviation Administration called for a nationwide ground stop that lasted 4.5 hours, the longest halt to US air travel since the attacks of September 11, 2001.

The spate of outages included a United Airlines technology failure on Monday that delayed about 150 flights on the same day that a JPMorgan Chase software problem disrupted some banking services.

On Tuesday, Apple said it was working to restore its systems after an internal update caused an outage that affected customer services including iCloud and Apple Pay. The issue was not caused by a cyberattack, Apple said.

Insurance provider Marsh also said on Tuesday its clients reported 105 cyber incidents in the last two weeks of October – more than double the 48 recorded in the final two weeks of May.

Experts worry that AI tools are feeding a surge of cyberactivity, with cybersecurity companies regularly turning up examples of hackers using AI to launch scores of intrusions at once.

"The recent string of major disruptions across industries highlights how deeply interconnected our digital infrastructure has become, and how a single technical failure or software update can cascade with outsized effects across critical systems," said Cynthia Kaiser, a former senior FBI cyber official and current senior vice president of cybersecurity firm Halcyon's Ransomware Research Center.

The string of tech outages is likely due to issues emerging from system upgrades, US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said in an interview with Fox Business on Tuesday.

"We do not see the indicia of a coordinated cyberattack... And we do not see the indicia of state-sponsored activity here. And we can be fairly confident in that," Clayton said.

He attributed the NSA outage to patches deployed for a PHP vulnerability discovered using AI last month – a bug that could let hackers remotely take control of servers.

"Everybody recognises it's time to upgrade their systems, and as they upgrade them, they're not coming back as expected in all cases, and in some cases, systems have to hand off to other systems, and those handoffs are not coming back as expected," Clayton told the "Claman Countdown" program on Fox Business. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Woods to return to PGA Tour after two years out
articles.excerpt: Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf for the first time in more than two years next month when he…
articles.fullText:
Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf for the first time in more than two years next month when he tees off at the Hero World Challenge event in the Bahamas, organisers said on Tuesday.

Woods, 50, was named in the line-up for the limited field PGA Tour event taking place in Albany from December 3-6.

It will mark the first time Woods has played an official PGA Tour event since July 2024.

The 15-time major champion has battled injuries and legal problems since his last appearance.

In March he was involved in a rollover car crash in Florida which led to him having his driver's license suspended for five years.

Authorities determined the 15-time major champion had not been drinking alcohol but found he appeared to be impaired.

Woods, who has undergone multiple back operations and surgeries on severe leg injuries suffered in a separate 2021 California car crash, had two pills containing the opioid painkiller hydrocodone in his pocket.

He refused a urine analysis and was charged, jailed and released on bond.

Woods initially pleaded not guilty to charges of DUI (driving under the influence) with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test.

Days later, he said he was "stepping away" to seek treatment and focus on his health.

Since the crash, Woods has travelled outside the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient facility, reportedly in Switzerland.

He made his first public appearance since his arrest at the PGA Tour's Travelers Championship in June, and later struck a plea agreement which led to his driver's license being suspended.

Woods has not won a tournament since a victory at the ZoZo Championship in Japan in 2019. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Norway, Portugal into Nations League quarter-finals
articles.excerpt: Erling Haaland fired Norway into the Nations League quarter-finals on Tuesday with a last-gasp penalty which completed a stunning comeback…
articles.fullText:
Erling Haaland fired Norway into the Nations League quarter-finals on Tuesday with a last-gasp penalty which completed a stunning comeback from two goals down to win 3-2.

Manchester City striker Haaland scored from the spot in the sixth minute of injury time in Copenhagen as Norway leapfrogged their hosts into second place in Group A, on head-to-head record as both teams finished on nine points.

Both teams ended the group stage six points behind winners Portugal, who got their first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era with a 3-2 success against Wales.

The winner was one of two goals from Haaland, who also started the fightback in the 37th minute – and had a goal disallowed – after early strikes from Rasmus Hojlund and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg gave Denmark a commanding lead in front of passionate support.

Haaland was given the chance to nick a spot in the last eight from the Danes, who only needed a draw to go through, after a handball from Joachim Andersen which was spotted by the VAR officials just as the hosts thought they had survived another in a series of scares.

Denmark had been on the back foot ever since Haaland halved the deficit when a howler from Denmark goalkeeper Mads Hermansen gifted possession to Martin Odegaard.

It was Odegaard who forced home Norway's leveller with six minutes remaining and set up a grandstand finish which was completed with Haaland's dramatic winner.

"This has been one of the craziest years in football I've ever experienced," said a relieved Haaland to TV2 in Norway.

Norway will join Portugal in Friday's draw in Nyon, where the four group winners will be seeded and each play against one of the four second-placed teams.

Haaland's winner made Portugal's win over Wales irrelevant to their group placing, but Carlos Forbs' classy strike in the 70th minute in Cardiff made sure of a positive finish for Jorge Jesus' team.

Forbs' first international goal decided a hugely entertaining encounter in which Wales, already guaranteed to finish bottom of the group, put in a performance which belied their position.

Wales will take part in the play-offs to decide the final promotion and relegation spots between Leagues A and B, and on Tuesday's evidence they have a fighting chance of staying in the top tier.

David Brooks quickly replied to Bruno Fernandes' superb opener for Portugal and Wales had their tails up when Sorba Thomas slid the hosts in front in the 40th minute.

But Pedro Neto, who was later sent off, almost immediately levelled the scores and Forbs decided an even contest and ensured Portugal would bounce back from a humiliating defeat at the hands of Denmark at the weekend.

"It's a special feeling; I won't forget today. The most important thing is that we managed to win," said Forbs.

"We needed the goal to calm the game down, and it just so happened that I scored."

Northern Ireland were promoted to League A for the first time after Justin Devenny's thumping strike gave his team the draw they needed against Hungary in Budapest.

Devenny, who plays for Stoke City in England's second tier, lashed home a beautiful strike in the 65th minute at the Ferenc Puskas Arena to level the match at 1-1 and secure a second successive promotion for Michael O'Neill's team.

"I feel amazing. I'm due one, that was my second for Northern Ireland. To see the game out, we dug deep and we've deserved it. We've had a great campaign and we can't wait for more," said Devenny to the BBC.

Republic of Ireland will join Wales in the play-offs after closing out Group B3 with a 3-0 win over 10-man Kosovo and moving into second place. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: States put speed-limiting devices in reckless drivers' cars
articles.excerpt: Virginia's GPS speed limiter program is already active for reckless driving offenders, but early users report glitches that apply wrong…
articles.fullText:
We've all seen it. You're driving down the highway when someone flies past you at a ridiculous speed. Maybe they're weaving through traffic while everyone else tries to stay out of their way. Now, states are turning to speed-limiting devices that could stop some of the most dangerous drivers from doing it again.
Virginia has already started installing GPS-powered devices in vehicles used by certain reckless-driving offenders. Washington, D.C., has a similar program, and more jurisdictions are exploring the technology. The idea sounds promising. Instead of simply telling someone to slow down, the device can actually restrict how fast their car accelerates.
However, there's a catch. Some drivers using these systems have reported GPS glitches that mistakenly apply the speed limits of nearby roads. And that raises a question worth asking. What happens when your car refuses to accelerate because its GPS thinks you're somewhere else?
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
SILICON VALLEY DEVELOPER ACCUSED OF MURDER AFTER INVESTIGATORS SAY TESLA REACHED 142 MPH BEFORE FATAL CRASH
The technology is called Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA). It uses GPS location information and digital maps to determine the posted speed limit. Here's how it works. Let's say you're traveling on a road with a 45 mph speed limit. As your vehicle reaches 45 mph, the device restricts additional acceleration. Pressing harder on the gas pedal won't normally make the car accelerate beyond that limit.
However, the system doesn't automatically slam on the brakes or shut off the engine. Instead, it limits the vehicle's ability to accelerate. That means a vehicle traveling downhill could still exceed the posted limit because of gravity.
Some systems also allow brief overrides when additional acceleration is necessary for safety. Think of it as a speed governor that automatically adjusts as you move between roads. The important difference comes down to control. Many newer vehicles already recognize speed limits and warn drivers when they're going too fast. These aftermarket devices take things further by restricting acceleration.
Virginia launched its Intelligent Speed Assistance Program on July 1. The state allows courts to require speed-limiting technology for certain driving offenses, including reckless driving and racing. The Virginia DMV can also require participation in qualifying cases involving excessive demerit points. For eligible drivers, the program offers a way to maintain restricted driving privileges rather than face a full license suspension. According to a Nov. 2 report, approximately 100 devices had been installed in Virginia since July. Many participants faced reckless-driving charges or convictions. Some cases involved speeds exceeding 100 mph.
The restrictions are serious. Qualifying drivers may need the equipment installed in every vehicle they own or co-own. They must also comply with restrictions on which vehicles they can operate. Then there's the cost. Participants generally pay installation and ongoing service fees, although financial assistance may be available for those who qualify. The goal is to let certain drivers continue essential travel while reducing the risk of dangerous speeding.
Virginia has company in exploring this approach. Washington, D.C. launched its Intelligent Speed Assistance Program on Oct. 1, 2025. Under the program, D.C. driver's license holders convicted of aggravated reckless driving must enroll and operate only authorized vehicles equipped with the technology .
Washington state passed legislation in 2025 requiring speed-limiting devices in certain cases involving dangerous speeding and driving restrictions. However, those requirements won't take effect until Jan. 1, 2029. Meanwhile, New York City is considering a proposal introduced on Oct. 22. It would require vehicle owners who accumulate 16 school-zone speeding violations within 12 months to install speed-limiting devices. The New York City proposal remains in committee and has not become law. These programs differ in scope. Still, they show how policymakers are increasingly considering technology as a response to dangerous driving.
JOE BIDEN MANDATED ALL NEW VEHICLES COME INSTALLED WITH A 'KILL SWITCH.' THIS REPUBLICAN WANTS TO REPEAL IT
GPS technology is incredibly useful. But anyone who's followed navigation directions onto the wrong road knows it can make mistakes. Consider this situation. You're driving on a highway with a 65 mph speed limit. A service road running alongside it has a 35 mph limit. If your GPS mistakenly places you on the service road, the speed limiter could apply the lower limit. Your vehicle wouldn't suddenly brake, but it could restrict additional acceleration even though you're traveling on a highway with a higher speed limit. That's the type of GPS problem some Virginia participants have reported.
Early users reportedly experienced situations where their devices applied lower limits from nearby roads. Officials acknowledged the complaints and said they were working on fixes. To be clear, the reports establish that location errors have occurred. They do not establish a pattern of crashes caused by those errors. That could become a safety concern when a driver needs additional acceleration to merge into traffic, but the vehicle won't respond as expected. That's a potential safety concern officials need to address before these systems become more widespread.
Some systems provide temporary overrides when drivers need additional acceleration. Virginia's proposed technical standards outline specific limits for emergency overrides, although those requirements have not yet been finalized. Under the proposal, an override would last no longer than 30 seconds, permit a maximum of 5 mph above the posted speed limit and allow no more than two overrides per driving cycle.
Those specifications appear in regulations published Oct. 19. The rules remain proposed, with public comments accepted through Dec. 18. The limits are intended to balance safety with the program's goal of preventing excessive speeding. However, they also show that an emergency override may provide much less acceleration than a driver expects. That's why clear instructions and reliable operation are so important.
There's a serious reason states are considering these devices. According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, 11,288 people died in speeding-related traffic crashes in 2024. Speeding contributed to 29% of all U.S. traffic fatalities that year. Those numbers help explain why officials want something more effective than another speeding ticket.
A driver who repeatedly ignores speed limits may continue taking risks after paying fines. And suspending someone's license doesn't physically prevent that person from getting behind the wheel. Speed-limiting technology offers another option. A properly functioning device can prevent certain excessive speeds while allowing qualifying drivers to continue traveling to work or handling essential responsibilities.
However, speed limits tell only part of the safety story. Someone can drive recklessly without exceeding the posted limit. Following too closely can still cause a crash. Bad weather can also make a legally permitted speed dangerous. So, these devices may help reduce extreme speeding, but they cannot guarantee safe driving.
NEW BIG RIG SAFETY TECH COULD SAVE YOUR LIFE
That's the bigger question. For now, these enforcement programs focus on drivers who meet specific legal criteria. There is no nationwide requirement forcing every U.S. driver to install one of these aftermarket speed-limiting devices. However, many newer vehicles already offer speed-limit recognition and warnings. That means some of the technology has become familiar to drivers.
The bigger step involves allowing software to actively restrict acceleration. As more jurisdictions test these programs, lawmakers could consider expanding eligibility. But any expansion would require additional policy decisions. And public acceptance could become a major obstacle. After all, there's a big difference between your dashboard warning you that you're speeding and your car preventing you from accelerating.
There's another issue I think deserves more attention. What happens to all the driving information these systems collect? GPS-based speed limiters need location data to determine which speed limit applies. Depending on the program, they may also record speeding events and other information used to monitor compliance.
Virginia's proposed regulations would require service providers to report certain vehicle events and speed violations, including GPS locations. The proposal also contains a significant additional requirement. Beginning July 1, 2027, new installations would need cameras capable of photographing the driver's seat when the device records a speeding event, if the proposed rules take effect as written.
That raises questions about who can access the information and how long it remains stored. We explored similar privacy concerns in our article, Is it worth saving money to let a car insurance company track your every move? Insurance tracking programs serve a different purpose. However, both technologies show how much information connected vehicles can generate about the people driving them. And once that information exists, clear rules about its collection and use become especially important.
I understand why states want to take this approach. We've all shared the road with someone driving so recklessly that you wonder how they still have a license. And if technology can prevent someone from driving 100 mph through traffic, I see the appeal. What concerns me is putting that much authority in the hands of a GPS system that can make mistakes. I've seen enough technology glitches over the years to know that even sophisticated systems sometimes get things wrong. That's inconvenient when your phone sends you to the wrong address. It's a much bigger concern when you're behind the wheel. I also think states need to be careful about how they expand these programs. Targeting repeat dangerous drivers makes sense. Requiring everyone to surrender control of their vehicle would raise a very different set of questions. Before we go further, I'd like to see stronger evidence that these devices reduce crashes without creating new safety problems. Because ultimately, the goal should be safer roads. And that means making sure the technology earns our trust before we depend on it.
Would you feel safer knowing reckless drivers have speed limiters in their cars, or does the idea of a GPS system controlling your accelerator worry you even more? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

articles.title: Working Holiday Scheme signed
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong and Chile today signed an agreement to establish a bilateral Working Holiday Scheme (WHS) for their youth. Secretary…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong and Chile today signed an agreement to establish a bilateral Working Holiday Scheme (WHS) for their youth.

Secretary for Labour & Welfare Chris Sun and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Chile Francisco Pérez Mackenna signed the agreement on the sidelines of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen. Chief Executive John Lee and President of Chile José Antonio Kast witnessed the signing.

Welcoming the agreement, Mr Sun said: “Chile is Hong Kong’s first WHS partner in Latin America. The scheme will provide young people from Hong Kong and Chile with opportunities to broaden their horizons and gain first-hand experience of living and working in a different cultural environment.”

Mr Pérez Mackenna said: “We are pleased to provide young people from Chile and Hong Kong with new opportunities to experience life in each other’s communities. Hong Kong’s unique blend of Eastern and Western cultures, international outlook and dynamic economy will offer Chilean youth an enriching experience. We also look forward to welcoming young people from Hong Kong to discover Chile’s rich culture, warm hospitality and natural beauty, thereby strengthening mutual understanding and people-to-people ties.”

Under the agreement, successful applicants can stay for up to 12 months in either Hong Kong or Chile. Participants may take up employment to finance their stay or enrol in short-term courses, subject to an annual quota of 100 places for each side.

This marks the 15th Working Holiday Scheme Hong Kong has established since 2001. Similar arrangements are already in place with New Zealand, Australia, Ireland, Germany, Japan, Canada, Korea, France, the United Kingdom, Austria, Hungary, Sweden, the Netherlands and Italy.

Over 109,000 Hong Kong youths have benefited from these schemes to date. Details on visa application procedures will soon be available on the websites of the Immigration Department and Chile’s National Migration Service .

articles.title: The VPN setting that keeps your printer and apps working
articles.excerpt: VPN split tunneling lets your banking app skip the encrypted tunnel while other apps stay protected, and the Allow LAN…
articles.fullText:
If you use a VPN , you've probably run into this at least once. You turn it on to protect your privacy, and suddenly something stops working. Maybe your printer won't connect. Maybe your banking app keeps asking you to verify your identity. Or perhaps a website refuses to load.
So you do what a lot of us would do. You turn off the VPN to fix the problem. Everything starts working again, and you forget to turn the VPN back on. That's the problem. You've disabled a privacy tool because it was getting in your way.
Fortunately, there's a setting that can help. It's called VPN split tunneling, and it lets you choose which apps use your VPN and which ones connect normally. There's also a separate setting worth checking if your printer stops working. Here's how both work and how to set them up with a VPN.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams , find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
TRAVEL MISTAKE PUTS PHONE, LAPTOP AND STREAMING ACCOUNTS AT RISK
A virtual private network, or VPN, encrypts your internet traffic between your device and the VPN server. It also hides your usual public IP address from the websites you visit. That added privacy can be especially useful on public Wi-Fi . However, some apps and websites don't always cooperate with VPN connections.
When you connect through a VPN, your bank may see an IP address associated with a different location or one shared by other VPN users. That can trigger additional security checks. Your bank might ask you to verify your identity again, block a login attempt or temporarily restrict access. The bank is trying to protect your account. Still, those interruptions can get frustrating when you're simply trying to check your balance or pay a bill.
Your printer works differently from your banking app. Most wireless printers communicate with your computer through your home Wi-Fi network. That connection typically stays inside your local network instead of traveling out to the internet. Some VPN settings can interfere with this communication, particularly when access to local devices is restricted.
The result? Your printer may suddenly appear offline even though it's connected to Wi-Fi and working normally. Here's the important distinction. Split tunneling can help with certain app connections, but printer problems often require a separate local network setting.
Think of split tunneling as giving certain apps permission to take a different route. Normally, when your VPN is connected, supported internet traffic travels through the encrypted VPN tunnel. With split tunneling, you can choose which apps or connections bypass that tunnel. For example, you might want your browser and email to continue using your VPN. However, if your banking app repeatedly triggers security checks, you could allow that app to use your regular internet connection.
Both types of connections can operate at the same time. That means you don't have to disconnect your entire VPN whenever one app has trouble. There is one trade-off to understand. Apps that bypass the VPN use your regular IP address and lose the extra privacy provided by the VPN tunnel. Secure websites can still encrypt their traffic using HTTPS, but your VPN no longer shields those excluded connections. For that reason, I recommend keeping most apps on the VPN and excluding only the ones that actually need it.
Many VPN services offer split tunneling, but not all of them include it. The available controls also depend on your device, operating system and VPN app. Some let you exclude individual apps, while others allow you to create rules for websites or IP addresses.
Before getting started, open your VPN app and look for a setting called Split Tunneling, App Exclusions or something similar. If you don't see one, check your VPN provider's support website to find out whether the feature is available for your device. Here's how the setup generally works across different platforms.
On Windows and Mac, some VPN apps let you choose which applications use the VPN and which connect directly to the internet. The exact steps depend on your VPN provider.
Some VPNs also let you create routing rules for specific IP addresses or websites. However, most people will find app-based controls easier to manage when they're available.
Keep in mind that split tunneling support varies on Mac. Some VPNs may require additional permissions, a particular connection protocol or an updated version of the app. If you can't find the setting, check your VPN provider's instructions before changing anything else.
SHOULD YOU USE A SEPARATE COMPUTER FOR ONLINE BANKING?
Android supports app-based VPN routing, and many VPN services offer split tunneling through their Android apps. However, the feature and its settings vary by provider.
If your VPN supports this type of split tunneling, the selected apps should use your regular internet connection while the remaining apps continue using the VPN.
One thing to watch for: Android has a system setting called Block connections without VPN. If you've enabled it, apps configured to bypass the VPN may lose internet access because Android blocks traffic that doesn't use the VPN.
Disabling that restriction can allow split tunneling to work, but it also changes your protection if the VPN connection drops. If you depend on that stricter security setting, consider leaving it enabled.
Here's an important difference for Apple users. Split tunneling options are generally more limited on iPhones and iPads than on Windows or Android devices. Many consumer VPN apps do not offer a way to choose individual apps that bypass the VPN.
Some VPN services may support certain network or IP address exclusions, but these features vary by provider. There is no universal setting on an iPhone that lets you select a banking app and automatically exclude it from your VPN connection.
Here's what to check:
There are limitations. Some VPNs support exclusions based on IP addresses rather than individual apps. Large websites and banking services often use multiple IP addresses that can change. As a result, excluding one IP address may not solve your problem.
Excluding public IP addresses can also create privacy risks because unrelated websites sometimes share the same network infrastructure. Avoid making these changes unless you understand which connections will bypass your VPN.
For most iPhone users, I recommend checking whether switching VPN servers resolves the problem before trying more advanced settings. If your VPN doesn't support split tunneling on iOS, you may need to use another troubleshooting method.
Linux users should also check their VPN app's settings. Some Linux VPN applications support split tunneling for individual apps or IP addresses, although the available features depend on the provider and Linux distribution.
3 VPN SETTINGS TO CHECK BEFORE YOUR NEXT TRIP
If your wireless printer stops responding while your VPN is connected, split tunneling may not be the first setting you need.
Some VPN services include an option that allows your computer or phone to communicate with devices on your local network, even while the VPN remains active. It may be called Allow LAN Access, Allow Local Network Access or something similar.
Here's what to look for on your device:
This setting can allow your computer to communicate with trusted devices on your home network while your VPN remains connected. Some VPN apps already permit local network access by default. Others may restrict it depending on your security settings, including certain kill switch configurations.
If you don't see a local network option, check your VPN provider's support instructions. The feature may use a different name or may not be adjustable in your version of the app.
One security tip: Only allow local network access when you trust the network. On public Wi-Fi , blocking communication with nearby devices can provide additional protection. If your printer still doesn't appear, check that both devices are connected to the same home network. Restart the printer and temporarily disconnect your VPN to see whether your computer can find it. This can help determine whether the VPN is causing the connection problem. Remember to reconnect your VPN after testing.
On a Mac, you can also try adding the printer manually using its IP address under System Settings > Printers & Scanners.
Split tunneling can help with banking app problems caused by VPN IP addresses, but it won't resolve every login issue. Before excluding your banking app, try connecting to another VPN server. Sometimes the problem involves a particular server address.
You can also check whether your banking service offers guidance about VPN connections. If you regularly encounter security checks, another option is a dedicated VPN IP address. Unlike a shared VPN address, a dedicated IP stays assigned to you. That consistency can reduce some verification requests without requiring you to bypass VPN protection.
Some VPN services offer dedicated IP addresses, either as part of certain plans or as an additional paid feature. Whatever you choose, don't disable your bank's security alerts or two-factor authentication to make logging in easier.
Here's what I like about this feature. You don't have to sacrifice your entire VPN connection because one app refuses to cooperate. Instead, you can make a targeted adjustment.
Your browser can continue using the VPN while an app that needs a direct connection bypasses it. And if the problem involves your home printer, you can check the local network access setting before changing anything else.
Just remember that excluded apps won't receive the same VPN protection. The idea is to make your VPN easier to use without unnecessarily giving up the privacy benefits you installed it for in the first place.
For the best VPN software, see my expert review of the best VPNs for browsing the web privately on your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.
I can understand why someone would turn off their VPN when a banking app won't open or a printer suddenly stops working. You want to get on with what you're doing. But I don't like the idea of turning off a privacy tool every time something goes wrong. That's why I think split tunneling is worth knowing about. If your VPN supports it, you can keep most of your internet traffic protected while making exceptions for apps that need a direct connection. And if you're having trouble printing, check that local network setting before doing anything else. Just be careful about which apps you exclude. I would rather make one small adjustment than leave my VPN turned off and forget about it.

articles.title: Alcaraz sweeps aside Tiafoe in ATP Finals opener
articles.excerpt: Carlos Alcaraz looked in ominous form on Monday as he began his bid to win the ATP Finals for the…
articles.fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz looked in ominous form on Monday as he began his bid to win the ATP Finals for the first time by cruising past Frances Tiafoe in straight sets, 6-2, 6-2.

World number three Alcaraz took just over an hour to deal with American Tiafoe and show why he is the favourite to win the whole thing in Turin, where he was the beaten finalist last year.

Since returning in August from a wrist injury that kept him off the tour for four months, Alcaraz has won three of the five tournaments he has entered, most recently the Paris Masters.

Alcaraz, 25, can book his place in the semi-finals on Wednesday by beating Italian Flavio Cobolli, who in the absence of former world number one Jannik Sinner is the crowd favourite.

"Sometimes I feel really comfortable," Alcaraz said.

"I feel like I'm better than the opponent in every aspect of the game.

"If I qualify to the semi-final or not, I think it's a great experience, a great week, getting experience," he added.

Tiafoe had a nightmare debut match at the season-ending tournament, the 28-year-old having no answer to Alcaraz's speed and power.

Only briefly in the second set did he look like challenging his opponent, a seven-time Grand Slam winner, when at 3-2 down he wasted three opportunities to break back. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Villagers in northern Laos are afraid to use river water after rare-earth pond spill
articles.excerpt: Government and Chinese-financed mining company say water is safe, but residents are skeptical after animal deaths.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Lao .
After ponds at a Chinese-financed rare-earth mining operation burst and potentially contaminated two rivers in northern Laos, villagers living downstream told Radio Free Asia they don’t think the water is safe.
Villagers in northern Laos fear using river water after drainage ponds at a Chinese-financed rare earth mine burst upstream from their communities.
On Nov. 1, several drainage ponds began to overflow at the Laos-China Rare Mineral Development Company North 2 Ltd. in Houaphanh province’s Xam Neua district. The water from the ponds drained into the Nam Vaen River, which flows into the Nam Xam River, which crosses the border into Vietnam.
There are approximately 18 affected villages that rely on the two rivers for agriculture, and this is the third rare-earth spill in the area after similar incidents in February 2024 and April 2026.
Authorities began an investigation on Nov. 4, consulting with officials from the mining company, who assured the government that the water was safe. But as early as Nov. 6, residents living downstream from the mining operation reported that fish were dying. Later, reports surfaced that birds and livestock like cows and pigs had also died. Authorities suspended mining indefinitely on Nov. 13.
A dead cow lies in the waters of the Nam Xam river in Houaphanh province, Laos, Nov. 13, 2026.
(Samakhom Khet 4) The local government should have visited the affected villages instead of just talking to the company, a resident of Muang Vaen village told RFA on condition of anonymity for security reasons.
“They say there is no contamination, telling the people to be confident that nothing is wrong, but right now, fish are dying in massive numbers,” the villager said. “They didn’t go inspect the downstream area where the incident happened – they didn’t come at all. They went to the site up at the top, listening to them, listening to the company at the project site saying ‘nothing is wrong, this and that.’ They’re just trying to keep people from panicking.”
During the investigation, the mining company told the government that the pond that burst was a natural water storage pond, not a chemical waste storage pond. The company stated it has repaired the water pipes and will compensate damages to two families whose rice fields were damaged, in accordance with the law.
The villager said the people still do not dare consume the water or even use it for household chores, despite the assurances from the provincial government that there is no issue and they can use the water as usual.
A map showing the location of the spill in Houaphanh Province, Laos.
(RFA) Shortly after the incident, an official of the Houaphanh Provincial Department of Agriculture and Environment told RFA that residents living downstream should temporarily stop using the water until inspection results are available and the problem is resolved.
Later, on Nov. 15, another official of the same department told RFA that authorities are currently investigating why the animals are dying.
“Right now, they have fixed it,” the second official said. “Currently, agricultural production can proceed, and the water can be used normally. As for the dead fish and other dead animals, they are still analyzing it.”
Foreign-invested farming, mining and development projects in Laos have sparked friction over cases of environmental pollution and land often taken without proper compensation, leaving villagers fearing retaliation if they speak out.
Skeptical residents
Residents have raised questions and demanded that relevant authorities conduct a serious investigation following state media reports clarifying that there was no chemical contamination of the water.
They also told RFA that they do not trust the Nov. 4 investigation, after which authorities announced that they found no severe impact and no dead aquatic animals, though there was still an issue with water concentration that might be caused by saltwater seepage from an old mining pit. The authorities at that time said they were waiting for official confirmation test results from the National Water Quality Research Institute.
But some of the residents have turned to mountain spring water, which is more difficult to collect, and is insufficient for their livelihoods, they told RFA. They do not trust the government because a similar incident occurred at the same mining operation in 2024. At that time the villagers tested the water themselves and found it was contaminated.
The rare earth mine developed by the Laos-China Rare Mineral Development Company North 2 Limited in Xam Neua district, Houaphanh province, Laos, is seen Feb. 27, 2024.
(Airbus) “Many villages are indirectly affected, so to speak – all 18 or 19 villages here,” a second villager told RFA on condition of anonymity to speak freely. “We cannot use the main river, the Nam Vaen.”
The villagers are demanding that authorities help them find replacement water to use for watering vegetables and agricultural production.
“Right now, for drinking and living water, it’s just mountain spring water and tiny streams, which isn’t enough to water vegetables and other crops,” the second villager said. “We are facing many hardships. They came to inspect and said nothing was wrong, yet we see so many dead fish there. Just like the previous time—when we took the water to get tested and we found contamination. When they took it to get tested, they didn’t find anything.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Fake E-ZPass email threatens $100 fine over unpaid toll
articles.excerpt: A fake E-ZPass email cites a real federal regulation to demand toll payments, but the law it references has nothing…
articles.fullText:
You open your email and see a warning from E-ZPass. Apparently, there's a problem with your toll account, and a payment didn't go through. Maybe you recently drove through a toll plaza. Maybe your credit card expired. Either way, it's the kind of message that makes you wonder whether you owe money. And that's exactly what scammers are counting on.
We recently received a convincing fake E-ZPass email claiming an overdue toll could trigger additional penalties and even affect your vehicle's registration renewal. The message includes familiar E-ZPass branding and an official-looking violation number. There's even a big purple "Pay Now" button. But take a closer look, and several warning signs point to a phishing scam.
And here's what I find especially interesting. The scammers behind this email even borrowed language from federal regulations to make their payment demands sound legitimate.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
FAKE AAA EMAIL SCAM TARGETS DRIVERS
The email arrived with a subject line reading "Your E-ZPass Account Has an Overdue Balance." The sender identified itself as "E-ZPass Violations Dept #276797." The message displayed the E-ZPass logo and included a violation reference number. It even listed Nov. 6 as the issue date. The headline gets straight to the point: "Your toll payment could not be processed." According to the message, a recent toll crossing could not be charged because of insufficient funds, a declined credit card or an expired payment method. That explanation sounds believable because payment problems can happen with legitimate toll accounts.
Then comes the pressure. The email warns that unpaid balances could be referred to collections. It also threatens a civil penalty of up to $100 per violation and a possible hold on vehicle registration renewal. To make those claims sound official, the message cites a federal regulation. Below the warning, the recipient sees a large "Pay Now" button. There are also options to update a payment method or dispute the alleged violation. The apparent goal is to scare someone into following a link that could lead to a fraudulent payment website. From there, scammers may try to steal credit card information or other sensitive details.
At first, this email looks like a legitimate toll notice . But once you start looking at the details more closely, several red flags suggest something is wrong. Here's what caught our attention.
One of the biggest clues appears in the email details. Although the message claims to come from E-ZPass, the actual sender address ends in @cashcoma.cooljz.com. The reply-to address also uses that unrelated domain. That's a major warning sign. Scammers can make the sender's display name say almost anything. They can also copy official logos to make their messages look convincing. However, the underlying email address can reveal something very different.
In this example, the recipient field also displays noreply@ezpassviolations.com. That might look official, but an address appearing in the "To" field says nothing about who actually sent the email. Even when an address looks familiar, it's worth checking. Criminals can spoof sender information to impersonate legitimate organizations.
At the top of the message, a notice says that if the email lands in your junk or spam folder, you should move it to your inbox. It also asks you to add the sender to your safe sender list. So, an email demanding payment is also asking you to override your email provider's spam warning.
Legitimate senders sometimes ask people to check their spam folders. However, in this case, the request appears alongside suspicious sender information and a threatening payment notice. The email had already landed in the junk folder. That alone doesn't prove fraud, but it gives you another reason to investigate before clicking anything .
This may be the most revealing detail in the entire email. The message references 23 CFR Part 940, suggesting federal regulations require drivers to settle outstanding toll balances under the conditions described in the notice. There's a big problem with that claim.
23 CFR Part 940 covers intelligent transportation system architecture and standards. It addresses how certain transportation technology systems are developed and implemented. It does not establish the blanket toll payment obligation suggested by this email. The reference to federal law gives the warning an appearance of authority, even though the cited regulation doesn't support the payment demand. And let's be realistic: how many of us would stop to look up a federal regulation while worrying about an overdue bill? That's what makes this tactic so concerning.
FAKE SOCIAL SECURITY STATEMENT EMAIL HIDES A SCAM
The email warns that you could face a $100 civil penalty, additional fees and even trouble renewing your vehicle's registration. That's enough to make anyone nervous, especially when the email doesn't even tell you how much you supposedly owe in tolls. And here's something else that caught my attention. There's no toll crossing location, no license plate number and no date showing when the alleged violation happened.
The email does include a violation reference number, but don't let that fool you. Scammers can easily make up a string of letters and numbers to make a message look official. Now, real toll violations can come with penalties, depending on the toll agency and its rules. But if an unexpected email suddenly threatens you with fines or registration problems, you should verify the claim directly with your toll agency before taking any action.
For years, many toll phishing scams arrived as text messages. Drivers would receive a warning about an unpaid balance, followed by a link demanding immediate payment. We previously reported on fake toll road texts targeting drivers across America . Those schemes directed victims to fraudulent payment websites designed to collect financial information. The email we reviewed uses a similar approach, but its polished appearance gives scammers another way to reach potential victims. The E-ZPass Group has warned about fraudulent emails and text messages impersonating toll agencies. It also explains that the E-ZPass Group itself does not hold customer accounts or collect toll payments. Individual member agencies handle those services.
The problem has become significant enough to show up in federal fraud data. In May, the Federal Trade Commission reported that government imposter scam reports rose 40% in 2025. The agency said bogus overdue toll notices contributed to that increase. Those messages often threaten additional fees or registration problems if drivers fail to pay quickly. It's a familiar tactic, but scammers continue to find ways to make their warnings more convincing. We reached out to the E-ZPass Group for comment on this particular email and to ask whether it has seen similar messages targeting drivers, but did not receive a response before our deadline.
A suspicious toll notice can catch you off guard, especially when it threatens fines or registration problems. Before you click anything or make a payment, here are a few simple steps I recommend taking to protect yourself.
Open the official website or app for your toll provider. Avoid using the payment button inside a suspicious email. Instead, sign in through the website you normally use. Look for outstanding balances or payment problems there. If you have questions, contact your toll agency using its published customer service number. For example, New York E-ZPass customers can visit E-ZPass New York at e-zpassny.com/. Other states and toll agencies operate their own official websites. If the email claims you have a violation, ask the agency to verify it using your account information.
Avoid clicking "Pay Now" or "Update Payment Method" in an email you cannot verify. A fraudulent payment page may look almost identical to the real website. Once you enter your credit card information, scammers could use it to make unauthorized charges. For more ways to recognize suspicious links, see our CyberGuy article on how to spot and prevent phishing attacks in your inbox.
Check the complete sender and reply-to addresses. Don't rely on the displayed name or logo. If you see unfamiliar domains or addresses that don't match the organization, treat the message as suspicious. Keep in mind that even a familiar-looking sender address can be spoofed. That's why independently verifying an unexpected payment request remains so important.
Take time to verify any warning about fines or registration problems. Scammers often use threats because fear can make people act without thinking. An alarming message deserves additional scrutiny, especially when it references legal consequences without providing enough information to verify the alleged violation.
IS THAT TRAFFIC TICKET TEXT A SCAM OR REAL?
Keep strong antivirus software installed and updated on your devices. Security software can help detect malicious websites and potentially harmful downloads. Some products also offer phishing protection that warns you when a link leads to a suspicious website. However, antivirus protection cannot guarantee that every fake payment page will be blocked. You still need to verify unexpected requests before sharing information. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.
Report the message as phishing through your email provider. You can also file a complaint with the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov or the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center at ic3.gov/. Include the suspicious sender address and details about the message. If possible, preserve the email until you've submitted your report. After reporting it, delete the message.
Reduce the personal information scammers can find about you online. Data brokers collect and sell information such as your name, address and phone number. Criminals can potentially use those details to make phishing messages more convincing. A data removal service can help remove your information from participating data broker websites, making it harder for scammers to find. While it won't stop every fake E-ZPass email, it can help reduce your exposure to targeted scams. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.
Accidentally clicked a link in a suspicious E-ZPass email? Don't panic. The next steps depend on what happened after you opened it. Here's how to protect yourself and limit any potential damage.
What really caught my attention about this scam was the reference to federal regulations. That's pretty clever on the scammers' part because most of us aren't going to look up a law when we're worried about an overdue bill. And the email looks polished enough that someone could easily overlook the strange sender address. I can see how someone might fall for it, especially if they've recently driven through a toll. My advice is to never pay an unexpected bill through a link in an email. Go directly to the toll agency and check your account. That extra step could save you a lot of trouble.
